articles.title: Fantasy Football: These NFL teams are dead in the water — but can we still trust their stars in our lineups?
articles.summary: Fantasy football analyst Chris Allen examines some bottom-barrel teams as we head into Week 11.
articles.body:
My wife and I were huge fans of "The Walking Dead" in its prime. She avoids scary movies like the plague. Yet, the drama kept us both locked in on Sundays until (spoiler alert) we lost Glenn. Afterward, we kept watching because it was our routine. But it didn't feel the same. And once we found something else, we never really noticed we had fallen behind on the show.

We've got several teams with the same vibe. Injuries or trades have erased any playoff hopes. And sure, there's still a player or two on the roster I'm looking to for fantasy production. But we need talent AND situation for that, and we don't have time to wait and see if things will change.

So, let's go through the teams that are (likely) dead and figure out which of their guys we can finally let go.

Honestly, speaking of "The Walking Dead," Arizona's roster probably looks like that group photo of the cast from Season 1 with most of the people grayed out because they were killed off during the show. The Cardinals have 14 players on IR. Jacoby Brissett is in Baltimore. And our lone ray of hope for Trey McBride is that Carson Beck immediately looked for him during his first start last Sunday.

There's a two-pronged, glass-half-full spin for McBride's value as we enter the Beck Era. First, all of his targets were first-read looks. Not a single throw from Beck to his TE1 took more than 2.2 seconds to get there. And, two, every single one of them was on the mark (100% catchable target rate). The problem was how every other facet of the offense operated.

CPOE: +0.9% (w/ Brissett), -9.4% (w/ Beck)

Granted, trying to avoid Aaron Donald and Braden Fiske carries its own challenge. But just 18 pass attempts will be what craters McBride's case to stay in the TE1 conversation. Jacoby Brissett threw the ball 20 times in his last game for Arizona. Sure, he wound up benched afterward, but McBride hasn't earned five targets in a single game since Week 16 of '24.

If you want to blame the schedule, I'll grant you that. Plus, the Cardinals have some easier matchups for Beck after their Week 14 bye (at NYJ, vs. NO, at LV). Accordingly, you could use the potential of improved environments for the Cardinals offense during the playoff stretch as a means to put McBride in a deal before the default deadline next week.

By and large, RBs are at the mercy of their QB's passing ability. All but four of the rushers with top-12 marks in red-zone touches come from top-12 squads in EPA per dropback. You need breakaway speed like Bijan Robinson or Jonathan Taylor to overcome a poor situation. That's not Rhamondre Stevenson's game. And New England's offensive ecosystem just took a turn for the worse.

Tommy DeVito didn't complete a pass farther than six air yards when he came in relief for Drake Maye. And I realize honing in on a single play misses some context around the entire performance. But DeVito didn't see other throwing windows anyway. Besides, that wasn't his only problem.

Pressure Rate: 48.4%, 3rd (highest rate of any single game for NE)

Without DE Aidan Hutchinson, the Lions were only able to get to DeVito soon after the snap on just a third of his dropbacks. But even when granted a clean pocket, he barely completed more than half of his attempts. The offense averaged 32.9 yards per drive with Maye during their gauntlet stretch of high-end defenses to start the year. It was down to 12.1 after he left the game.

That's why I'd be looking to move Stevenson. Corey Kiner's expanded role is just icing on the cake. He was already taking a third of the carries during the month prior. Stevenson's only upside was as a receiver. But if the Patriots have a bad backup QB and a tough schedule on the horizon (Bills in Week 13, Vikings, Chiefs), I'd rather let somebody else take on the risk.

So, let's apply the same process I laid out for the Patriots to the Dolphins. Essentially, we'll evaluate Miami's passing attack with Kyle McCord running the show as a means to gauge Ollie Gordon II's outlook. Right away, things look better down south.

Before you call me on trying to lead the witness, I know McCord had a strip-fumble gaffe that turned into six points for the Colts. But he also used his legs to score on a QB draw to cancel things out. Plus, as the above clip emphasizes, McCord pushed the ball farther downfield and took fewer sacks. Remember that 12.1 YPD metric for DeVito? McCord was up to 27.5. Overall, we can put the Dolphins' passing game ahead of New England's. Now, let's look at Gordon's workload.

Rushing Share (since Week 4): 71%, 9th (out of 30 RBs – min. 150 snaps)

At 17.8 carries per game, Gordon has one of the strongest opportunity shares in the league. Only James Cook III has seen a higher stacked box rate on early downs than Gordon (46.8%), but the Dolphins' RB1 isn't lagging too far behind in adjusted yards after contact per attempt (3.79 vs 3.15) or rushing success rate (46.3% vs 39.4%). And outside of Denver, no rushing defense on Miami's schedule should give you pause. Unless I could get similar RB2 value for Gordon, I'd keep him.

Let me flip the script when talking about Omarion Hampton. He put up his best performance of the season against the Ravens. More importantly, there were enough elements on tape to make the case that we can see something similar in the future.

Hampton has just five carries that have gained 15 or more yards. Kaelon Black, Christian McCaffrey's backup, has the same total. Anyway, two of those five from Hampton came on Monday night. But it wasn't just because the offensive line opened up a couple of holes. Baltimore met Hampton at or behind the LoS on 63.6% of his carries. He responded with a season-high 4.45 adjusted yards after contact per attempt. But we know efficiency can fluctuate between games. If I had a choice, I'd rather the volume hold.

OC Mike McDaniel finally came (back) around to the idea that letting Hampton lead the backfield was the best option. The line still needs to improve (0.8 yards before contact per attempt), but getting his RB1 into a rhythm has its merits.

Three of the Chargers' next six opponents are inside the top 10 in PPG allowed to rushers. The same number of defensive fronts are below the league average in pressure rate, giving Justin Herbert more time in the pocket and keeping the offense on schedule. If you could acquire Hampton off the 3-7 or 4-6 team without sacrificing much, I'd send out an offer for him.

Let's be real for a minute. The Colts underperforming was a risk we all accepted when drafting Jonathan Taylor. Daniel Jones was coming off of the Achilles reconstruction. Alec Pierce's health was in question even during the summer. Admittedly, a franchise-altering implosion wasn't easy to see, but Taylor maintaining his workhorse status was the bet we made in the first round. Indianapolis pulled the rug out from under us two months later.

Unfortunately, Taylor didn't lose his shoe , leading to another high-value touch for Seth McGowan against the Dolphins. And it wasn't the first time we had to question the workload for their (and our!) RB1. Since Indianapolis opened its doors for business, we've seen less of Taylor in the role we got used to back in September.

Snap Rate: 80% (before Nelson trade), 67% (since the trades)

Even in TNF to start Week 11, McGowan took 27.6% of the snaps with four touches to Taylor's 10. McGowan primarily played on long-down-and-distance scenarios, but they nearly split the targets (2 to 1), and both were on the field for half of the Colts' red-zone plays. It took a hamstring for McGowan to put Taylor back in the driver's seat.

Taylor was ninth in explosive run rate and one of 10 RBs with a double-digit target rate through Week 6. Simply put, he could overcome a poor environment. But as the Colts look to either preserve Taylor for the offseason trade market or evaluate the rest of the roster, moving on from the RB1 should be in your plans.

articles.title: Fantasy Football: Jaylen Waddle finally shows up, Bears' backfield goes off and more bold predictions for Week 11
articles.summary: Our Yahoo analysts share their one bold call for fantasy football in Week 11.
articles.body:
There aren't many weeks left in the fantasy football regular season; you can't hold anything back. That means you need to be bold to come out on top. Our Yahoo analysts share their one bold prediction for fantasy football in Week 11.

Jaylen Waddle turns in second WR1 finish of '26

I realize that trusting any WR tied to Bo Nix is like playing with fire. But there have been some fantasy-related improvements to Denver's passing game. First, Nix is throwing more relative to expectations. He's been at a +3.0% PROE over the last month, a 180-degree flip from Weeks 1-4 (-2.5%). He's also throwing to the middle of the field, where passing efficiency jumps, at the sixth-highest rate. And he's fifth in EPA per dropback on those throws.

That's where Jaylen Waddle comes into play. He's led the Broncos in targets on concepts over the MoF (2.49 YPRR). That's where the Raiders have been consistently beaten on defense. Opposing WRs are averaging 87.6 YPG and a smooth 24.8 PPR PPG on those throws alone. While both were on broken plays, both Seahawks' WRs found themselves in the end zone with the ball on throws between the numbers. Assuming Waddle clears protocol, he'll give us his second WR1 performance of the season in Week 11. — Chris Allen

Swift, Monangai both finish as top-12 fantasy RBs

The Bears' backfield will finally be at full strength in Week 11 with Kyle Monangai returning after a five-game absence due to a toe injury. He's picked the right defense to get back on the field against, since the Saints are allowing the second-most fantasy points to RBs, the eighth-most rushing yards and the fourth-most rushing touchdowns. Chicago also has an implied total of 30 points, so we can project a lot of scoring from Ben Johnson's crew.

New Orleans has let 11 different backs reach double-digit fantasy points, including three sets of teammates. One of those duos was Bijan Robinson and Brian Robinson Jr., who both finished as top-12 fantasy RBs in Week 4. Monangai and D'Andre Swift also accomplished that feat in the opener versus the Panthers, which was one of the four games they've shared the field together this season. Get ready for them to do it again, now that the bar is lower with six teams on bye. — Justin Boone

Chig Okonkwo finishes as a top-5 fantasy TE

Over the last month, Chig Okonkwo has the seventh-best TE volume and a top-5 route share when accounting for his Week 10 injury. He still has the big-play ability he's had throughout his career and can turn his volume into better production against a Bengals defense ranking bottom-5 versus TEs. Cincinnati is forcing opposing offenses into going pass-heavy, is able to slow down receivers on the outside, but has still allowed the second-most yards on the fourth-most targets to TEs inside, without playing against any of the top fantasy tight ends. If Okonkwo has the ball in his hands that much, he's bound to make some big plays after the catch. — Joel Smyth

Cam Ward finishes as a top-10 fantasy QB against Dallas

I know Cam Ward's name hasn't exactly been synonymous with fantasy scoring, but he's quietly put together two pretty damn good games. Dallas, meanwhile, has been loudly awful on defense for more than two seasons. New defensive play-caller this week? Cool. I'm still calling a top-10 finish for Ward. He's thrown for 535 yards and four touchdowns over his last two games and added another 80 yards on the ground. Dallas is giving up 7.8 yards per pass attempt and has already allowed 19 passing touchdowns. Brock Purdy just hung 389 yards and three scores on them in 28 attempts. Ward doesn't have to do all that. Give me 250 through the air, two touchdown passes and another 35 on the ground. And if Dak Prescott gets Dallas out to an early lead, good. That's more chances for Ward to throw against a defense I'm still going out of my way to attack. — Ray Garvin

Tony Pollard has six catches or 80 yards receiving (or both)

The Titans normally don't throw the ball much to Pollard, but that's changed in the last three games — the underrated back has collected 14 catches in that span. And the Dallas defense is especially terrible when it comes to tracking running backs in the passing game — Christian McCaffrey had a field day against this unit last week. Tennessee's offense has been up to code in the last three weeks, and this game features a 54.5-point total. Pollard is going to crush in his revenge game against the Cowboys, and part of the story will be written through the air. — Scott Pianowski

Christian McCaffrey catches double-digit passes

On the surface, maybe this doesn't sound bold but funny enough, McCaffrey has done this just once in over 60 regular and postseason games with the 49ers. It happened last season when he caught 10 passes against the Cardinals in a low-scoring game. The 49ers lead the league in getting five players out in the route, accounting for 75% of their dropbacks. That's unlikely to change against Minnesota and its blitz looks. I expect McCaffrey to be heavily involved as a receiver in the flats, as an escort screen option and on extended checkdowns. There will be voids in coverage against Minnesota there and Brock Purdy has been excellent at picking the right spots to attack. — Matt Harmon

articles.title: Why WWE star Damian Priest believes the Judgment Day deserves a spot in the WWE Hall of Fame
articles.summary: WWE star Damian Priest believes that the Judgment Day has done enough to earn a place in the WWE Hall of Fame, despite no longer associated to the faction.
articles.body: WWE star Damian Priest believes that the Judgment Day has done enough to earn a place in the WWE Hall of Fame, despite no longer associated to the faction. The former Judgment Day member Damian Priest has spoken highly of his former group and feels they deserve a spot in the Hall of Fame.Over the years, the Judgment Day has established and grown in the company substantially despite other groups disbanding around them. The former World Heavyweight Champion recently reflected on his time with the group and explained why he believes it will be remembered as one of the greatest factions in professional wrestling history. Let's take a closer look at why Damian Priest believes that The Judgment Day earns a spot in the Hall of Fame.WWE star Damian Priest reflects on why The Judgment Day deserves to be in the Hall of FameWWE star and former The Judgment Day faction member believes that the group has done enough to earn a place in the WWE Hall of Fame, despite no longer being part of the faction.The former World Heavyweight Champion recently reflected on his time with the group and explained why he believes it will be remembered as one of the greatest factions in professional wrestling history. He reflected on the group's most successful run and highlighted how multiple members simultaneously held championship gold in WWE.During an appearance on the Complex Graps podcast, Priest opened up about the faction's formation, its remarkable championship success and the bond shared by its members. He also admitted that he once expected to remain part of The Judgment Day for the rest of his WWE career."I hoped [the Judgment Day would last this long], you know, but then again, I thought I was going to be in the Judgment Day forever. A group that I helped create, you know, it started with Edge, but you can't have a group of one person. So it was me and Edge," said Priest on Complex Graps.The faction initially took shape in 2022 under WWE Hall of Famer Edge and the former world champion revealed how he had planned to bring in each of the future members, including Rhea Ripley, Finn Balor, Dominik Mysterio, and JD McDonagh. He spoke about the special time he spent in the group, when several members held titles at the same time.Explaining the same, "That's one of those things that when we were running strong too, it was like we knew sometimes you don't know how special something is, but when we had all those titles, I was Señor Money in the Bank, undisputed tag champ, Rhea's the world champ, Dom, I think, was the North American champ. We were just looking at each other in our clubhouse and you're saying, 'We're it. This is real. We're probably all going to be in the Hall of Fame individually, but we're going to be in the Hall of Fame because of this group as well.'"During that run, Priest held the Money in the Bank briefcase and the Undisputed WWE Tag Team Championship. Ripley was the Women's World Champion, while Dominik Mysterio also enjoyed championship success as NXT North American Champion. Priest also explained that the members understood they were part of something special while looking back at their collective accomplishments.The Judgment Day has undergone considerable changes since Priest's departure, with the faction continuing its run without one of its original members. articles.title: Mikel Arteta Gives David Raya Injury Latest
articles.summary: On November 21, in the 17:30 kick-off, Arsenal travelled to St James’ Park to face Newcastle and ultimately had to settle for a point. The Gunners also exper...
articles.body:
On November 21, in the 17:30 kick-off, Arsenal travelled to St James' Park to face Newcastle and ultimately had to settle for a point. The Gunners also experienced a further setback, with David Raya having to leave the game early with what looked like a shoulder injury. Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta gave his initial thoughts on that injury during his post-match press conference .

Mikel Arteta Gives Injury Update on David Raya

Arsenal began the game on top and looked comfortable, with Newcastle struggling to impose themselves on the game. Bruno Guimaraes was unsurprisingly booed every time he touched the ball. Newcastle had one chance in the first half, but Arsenal finally got their deserved lead, with Eberechi Eze finishing coolly after a swift attack from the Gunners.

In the second half, the home side rallied and equalised through Harvey Barnes, before Malik Thiaw put his team 2-1 in front, sending the St James' Park faithful into a frenzy. Arteta's team showed their battling qualities and earned a point through a well-taken Noni Madueke goal, with 12 minutes to go.

During the second half, Raya collided with William Osula as he looked to launch an attack, but following treatment, the Arsenal no.1 was still in pain and was replaced by back-up goalkeeper Kepa. Speaking to the media after the match, Arteta was asked about Raya's condition and said:

"Unfortunately, he had to come off, which is not good news. He will have an MRI assessment tomorrow, but at the moment I don't know."

It remains to be seen just how serious the injury to David Raya is. Yes, Arteta doesn't say much, but it doesn't sound great. There was no talk about precaution or any glimmer of hope that it might not be serious. With a busy upcoming period for the Gunners leading up to Christmas, missing their influential number one will be a huge blow.

He's a vital member of this team and was a cornerstone of their success last season. He commands his area with aplomb, is exceptional with the ball at his feet, and some of the saves he's made for the Gunners have been staggering. He's one of the best goalkeepers in Europe, and all connected with Arsenal will be hoping the MRI brings good news, but looking at how uncomfortable he looked, and listening to Arteta, it does sound like there could be a period on the sideline for the Spanish goalkeeper.

articles.title: Steelers Get Bad News on Michael Pittman
articles.summary: PITTSBURGH — Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver Michael Pittman Jr. (left foot) will sit out another week. He will be inactive […]
articles.body:
PITTSBURGH — Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver Michael Pittman Jr. (left foot) will sit out another week. He will be inactive for Sunday's game against the Philadelphia Eagles, according to Brooke Pryor of ESPN .

Pittman was a full participant at Thursday and Friday's practice, after being limited on Wednesday while trying to return to action.

Pittman 21-day practice window opened on Wednesday.

Pittman said Wednesday that he wants to make sure he's effective when he's back out there. If he's feeling good, he believes he can make a difference by "just being out there when I'm needed," Pittman said. "Just those opportunities out there, just creating plays, throw some nice blocks and just play hard. Just bring that physicality and just someone that the guys can depend on. And just be there for any situation. If it's a 'run the ball' type game, hey, I'm in there to block safeties and linebackers."

Mike McCarthy said last week that Pittman was close to returning. Pittman was placed on injured reserve on Saturday, Oct. 10.

With injuries at receiver, the Steelers have relied on a smashmouth approach using tight ends Pat Freiermuth and Darnell Washington .

"I think that definitely has something to do with the amount of guys that we have down — Ben (Skowronek), me, Rome (Wilson)," Pittman said. "So probably a lot more 12 (personnel) just naturally. And we've got two tight ends who are very talented."

In addition to the 21-day practice day window opening for Pittman, the window also opened for wide receiver Roman Wilson , guard Gennings Dunke r and wide receiver Max Hurleman.

Wilson (left hand) will be active after being listed as questionable. Dunker (knee) is questionable for Sunday.

Alan Saunders and Brendan Howe provided reporting from Pittsburgh.

articles.title: Ithaca's Bercuvitz runs to third at NY Federation XC Championships
articles.summary: A third-place finish from Ithaca's Tsadia Bercuvitz led Section 4 runners at the NY Federation Cross Country Championships.
articles.body:
Ithaca High senior Tsadia Bercuvitz finished third in the girls race at the New York Federation Cross Country Championships on Saturday, Nov. 21, at Bowdoin Park in Wappingers Falls.

Bercuvitz, runner-up in this race last year, posted a 5,000-meter time of 18 minutes, 17.9 seconds. Maddie Laezza of East Port-South Manor won in 18:00.0, and Riley Lynch of Shenendehowa took second in 18:09.3.

Her effort helped Ithaca place 18th in the team standings with a total of 427. Northport won with a score of 117.

Other top Section 4 girls finishes: Ithaca's Mattea Dauria 75th in 20:11.8, Maine-Endwell's Madison Novotny 92nd in 20:24.6 and Ithaca's Avery Whittaker 106th in 20:39.2.

Bercuvitz was coming off a third-place finish in the Class A race at last week's New York State Public High School Athletic Association Championships at Queensbury High School.

Corning junior Christopher Lawson finished 13th in the Federation boys race with a time of 16:20.7 after capturing the Class A state title at the NYSPHSAA Championships. Ryan Sykes of Horace Greeley won in 15:13.8, with Class A public schools runner-up Brady Petrella second in 15:40.9.

Lawson's effort helped Corning finish fifth in the team standings with a score of 287. East Aurora won the title with a score of 144.

Chenango Valley senior Nikhil Datta placed 16th in 16:21.6 for the second-best finish among Section 4 boys.

Other top Section 4 boys: Corning's Graham Wightman 49th in 16:54.2, Vestal's Tyler Hayes 56th in 16:56.8, Susquehanna Valley's Aidan Skuban 60th in 16:58.4, Afton/Harpursville/Bainbridge-Guilford's Owen Degan 82nd in 17:08.9, Corning's Ashtyn Stark 107th in 17:24.5, Johnson City's Connor Smith 114th in 17:26.3 and Vestal's Kevin Middendorf 122nd in 17:28.5.

articles.title: Mets insider explains why A.J. Ewing $95 million extension is ‘big deal’
articles.summary: As rumors surround the New York Mets in the offseason connected to Tarik Skubal, the team has been making other key moves, such as signing A.J. Ewing to a l...
articles.body:
As rumors surround the New York Mets in the offseason connected to Tarik Skubal, the team has been making other key moves, such as signing A.J. Ewing to a long-term deal. With the Mets locking down Ewing to an eight-year, $95 million contract extension, this team insider explains how the deal is a key move for the team this offseason.

The 22-year-old stood out in his rookie season in New York, playing well at center field while hitting a .252 batting average with 11 home runs, 43 RBIs, and 23 stolen bases in 120 games. As Ewing is among the young core of the Mets along with Nolan McLean and Carson Benge , SNY insider Chelsea Jane would explain why the extension is a "big deal" for the team.

"They have not signed a player to a pre-arb deal like this since a guy named David Wright, and this one is bigger than that," Jane said. "It's a big deal also because it's a reminder of how much their system has produced in recent years. A.J. Ewing wasn't even the headliner of last year's rookie class…He came up. He played like a Gold Glove center fielder. He showed flashes of being the leadoff man of the future, navigated some ups and downs, and some growth. He's 22 years old. This deal buys out his pre-arb years, his arb-years, and gets him into free agency, and that's a big deal for the Mets."

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Why the Mets' signing A.J. Ewing is huge

Jane continued, saying that it's big news for the Mets since it resembles how president of baseball operations David Stearns operated with the Milwaukee Brewers when he was there from 2015 to 2023. Emphasizing the need to build up young talent and build around it, Jane says that's what New York has done with Ewing, and is on track to do so with McLean and Benge.

"But if they have the opportunity to do those deals, people I've talked to say they'll do them," Jane said. "So a really nice day for the Mets here."

At any rate, the Mets look to improve this offseason after finishing with a 74-88 record.

articles.title: Ferris State football wins 42nd straight after national TV spotlight
articles.summary: Ferris State football won its 42nd straight game, this time over Truman State, in the first round of the NCAA Division II playoffs.
articles.body:
BIG RAPIDS – Maybe, it was a Big Noon hangover.

After hosting Fox's "Big Noon Kickoff" pregame show outside of Top Taggert Field – the first time a college pregame show broadcast from a Division II school – the Ferris State Bulldogs came out sluggish in their first-round NCAA playoff game against Truman State on Saturday, Nov. 21.

The No. 1-ranked and two-time defending national champion Bulldogs made mistakes, blew a couple scoring opportunities and had a fumble, as Truman State took a 6-3 lead into the second quarter.

But as crews were tearing down the Fox set, the Bulldogs came alive, rolling to a 45-14 victory in front of 8,630 fans, their biggest crowd of the season.

Ferris will play Findlay in the second-round game in Big Rapids on Saturday, Nov. 28. Findlay won its first-round game by beating Augustana, 23-20, by kicking a field goal in overtime to advance. Grand Valley State also advanced, and would meet rival Ferris in the quarterfinals if both win next Saturday.

The Bulldogs were led by Chase Carter, a junior quarterback from Orlando, who completed 18 of 29 passes for 212 yards and two touchdowns. He also led the team in rushing with 17 carries for 93 yards.

Tarik Bower, a sophomore wide receiver from Corunna, caught five passes for 72 yards. And Taariik Brett, a senior, caught five passes for 42 yards and ran it four times for 72.

Trace Corlew, a sophomore defensive back from Gladwin, led the Bulldogs with 10 tackles. And Ryan Ahern, a sophomore linebacker from Rockford, added seven tackles.

Ferris State held Truman State to 80 yards rushing and 146 yards passing. Truman State quarterback Dylan Hair completed 11 of 20 passes for 146 yards with a touchdown and interception.

The Bulldogs have now won 42 consecutive games, an NCAA Division II record − Ferris State's last loss came Aug. 31, 2024, in its 2024 season opener to Pittsburg State (Kansas).

And Ferris has won four of the past five D-II national titles.

"It's great coaches," Ferris State coach Tony Annese said on the pregame show. "I've had two coaches that've been here since I've been here since in 2012, and then it's great players. It's recruiting, getting good players here. We've got something like 28 kids from Florida, so we go all over the nation to get recruits. And then it's player development. It's absolutely 100% player development."

The D-II national championship game is Dec. 19 at 4 p.m. ET in McKinney, Texas.

The Bulldogs are attempting to become the second D-II program with three straight titles, joining North Alabama in 1993-95.

articles.title: Lusty hat-trick helps Larne close gap at the top
articles.summary: Matty Lusty is the hat-trick hero as Larne produce a dominant display to see off Ballymena United and close the gap on the top two in the Irish Premiership.
articles.body:
Matty Lusty was the hat-trick hero as Larne produced a dominant display to see off Ballymena United and close the gap on the top two in the Irish Premiership.

Earlier in the day both leaders Linfield and second-placed Coleraine stretched their advantage over the reigning champions thanks to wins over Limavady United and Carrick Rangers respectively.

The Inver Reds rose to the challenge against their east Antrim neighbours and never looked back after Lusty put them in front in the 23rd minute.

The young striker doubled his and Larne's tally five minutes into the second half before Jordan McEneff made it 3-0 on 62 minutes.

Four minutes later, Lusty rounded off an impressive night's work with his third to seal the points and keep pace with the leaders as well as leaving the sorry Sky Blues just one point off the relegation play-off spot.

The opening quarter of an hour was largely forgettable as both sides struggled to get in behind their opponent.

A terrific slide rule pass from McEneff in the 16th minute finally bisected the rigid Sky Blues defence with Lusty cutting the ball back from the byeline only for the well-positioned David Toure to head away the ball.

That seemed to jolt the home side into action with only a great tackle by Stephen Fallon preventing Leroy Millar from getting a shot away on goal minutes later.

The pressure finally told in the 23rd minute as Larne cut through Ballymena once more with Millar laying the ball on a plate for Lusty to fire home from six yards.

The hosts looked to be able to slice through their opponents at will, and but for a fantastic tackle by Toure just past the half hour, Lusty would have been in on goal.

Lusty was denied again in the 43rd minute as the frontman got on the end of Aaron Donnelly's low drive across the face of goal, but Walsh did well to block the close range effort.

A minute later, the visitors thought they had got back on level terms following a scramble in front of the Larne goal with Glynn eventually forcing the ball home, but it was quickly ruled out for offside.

Shortly after the restart, Lusty grabbed his and Larne's second of the game as the hosts ripped through the Sky Blues rearguard once more.

Kevin O'Hara eased past Glynn before crossing for the onrushing Lusty to finish past Walsh from eight yards.

Chris McKee should have halved the deficit five minutes later after Caoimhin McConnell picked him out at the far post, but he failed to direct his header on goal.

That was to prove vital as Larne added a third on 62 minutes, as O'Hara turned provider once again, picking out McEneff after getting to the byeline and the midfielder applied the telling finish past Walsh.

Four minutes later, Lusty wrapped up his hat-trick, walking through a Ballymena defence claiming for an offside which never came before slamming the ball past the helpless Walsh to complete an impressive night's work.

articles.title: Everything Tom Izzo said after MSU's win over Detroit Mercy
articles.summary: See what Michigan State head coach Tom Izzo had to say about his team's win over Detroit Mercy.
articles.body:
Michigan State basketball defeated Detroit Mercy on Saturday afternoon, 91-70, improving to 5-1 on the season. The Spartans were able to win the game without both Coen Carr and Jordan Scott, although it was not pretty.

Another major storyline in this matchup was Tom Izzo going up against his former assistant coach Mark Montgomery, who is in his third season as the Titans head coach.

In his post game interview, Izzo not only commented on Montgomery and his program, but also gave his unfiltered thoughts on the Spartans performance on Saturday.

"I got a bit of what I deserved. I made some decisions that I think were still the right decisions, but I made some decisions where I don't know the maturity of my team and didn't know how they would take it."

"When you play guys 15, 20, 25 minutes, it becomes hard to sustain"

"The APR is a joke, it's a joke. You can't have APR when players can leave whenever."

"The ironic part of all this, Mark Montgomery was an academic All Big Ten player."

"We did not play very well. The lineups I had in there, Jesse got in foul trouble early. It was nice to see Carlos bounce back, to see Kur hit those shots. The hockey 'star of the game' was Jeremy Fears. It wasn't the 17 points. It was him in the huddle."

"He played like an All-American today. I've been here, you know I don't say that often."

"We got the boxing-I mean, hockey game tonight that I plan on going to."

"Jeremy (Fears) actually missed three free throws, which is illegal."

"I'm not giving up on my bigs yet. They are going to challenged this week. Arkansas is very tall in the middle."

"It was my decision. Those guys wanted to play. I was the wicked witch."

"What you saw today isn't Michigan State basketball, either."

"Guys got to play with more emotion, more passion. When you are not playing well, you play nervous. We just did not communicate with people."

"I'm hoping it lifts Kur Teng, that was his first big game since injury. The play of the game was halftime. Jeremy of old would take that in and try to get fouled, kicked it to Kur."

"I was more impressed with Jeremy since I have been since the day he got here. Hats off to Jeremy, I might have to be mad at him next week but love him to death today."

"I want to see the passion, the grit, that's what I have to work for."

"If you ask me, Cam (Ward) had the opportunity for a 20 (point), 15 (rebound) game."

"This week, there will be an emphasis on the bigs. They have to get better, they can get better, they will get better."

articles.title: Packers LT Jordan Morgan wearing cast on hand ahead of matchup with Myles Garrett
articles.summary: Packers LT Jordan Morgan was seen wearing a cast on his left hand at Saturday's practice.
articles.body:
Green Bay Packers left tackle Jordan Morgan might have only one fully healthy hand ahead of a matchup with All-Pro edge rusher Myles Garrett in Week 12.

Video of Saturday's practice from Bill Huber of Packers on SI showed Morgan, the team's starting left tackle, wearing a cast to protect his left hand or wrist while going through drills.

It's unclear when Morgan would have suffered the injury. He played all 55 snaps for the Packers offense in a loss to the Minnesota Vikings in Week 10, and the Packers have been off -- while on the bye week -- during Week 11. Matt LaFleur's team is practicing on Saturday to ramp up for a Wednesday night game in Los Angeles.

Morgan, in his first season as the starting left tackle, has allowed 24 total pressures across 429 pass-blocking snaps, per PFF. Among the 11 pressures allowed are five sacks and six quarterback hits, but Morgan has allowed only one sack and one quarterback hit over the last five games.

Two healthy hands or not, Morgan will face a big test on Wednesday night in Garrett, an All-Pro who set the NFL's single season sack record last season. Garrett has played in only three games since joining the Rams via trade, but he did produce 3.0 sacks in his first game back from injured reserve in Week 9.

Who is the Packers' backup left tackle? John Williams, who played the last three games at center, got the majority of the reps behind Morgan at left tackle during the preseason. Sean Rhyan practiced on Saturday, potentially freeing up Williams to be the backup for Morgan against the Rams.

Check the team's first injury report of Week 12 for more information on Morgan's injury.

articles.title: Jerry Jones says Cowboys had 'no record' of fight incident that resulted in fan's death at home loss vs 49ers
articles.summary: Jerry Jones says the Dallas Cowboys had no record of an incident before a fan died after their 49ers game at AT&T Stadium, pledging to investigate.
articles.body: Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones said Friday that the team had no record of an alleged fight that resulted in a fan’s death during the team’s game against the San Francisco 49ers, adding that he believed the fan was hospitalized because he "didn’t feel good" at the game—a claim that has raised questions about what happened at AT&T Stadium. Police say Mario Narro fell during a fight at the stadium. According to reports, he remained at the game but later complained to friends of pain. Paramedics at AT&T Stadium treated Narro before he was transported to a hospital, where he died Wednesday, his family says. Jones addressed the death during his Nov. 20 appearance on 105.3 The Fan’s "K&C Masterpiece," saying he had only just received information about the situation. COWBOYS OWNER JERRY JONES UPDATES TIMELINE FOR NFL'S 18-GAME SCHEDULE, FLOATS PRESEASON REDUCTION "No record of an incident at the game, and I just got that information... so we had no record of an incident, and we'll be obviously looking into that," Jones said, when asked about the Arlington Police Department's report of a fight that allegedly occurred around kick-off time. Jones added, "My understanding is that the individual went to the game, and didn't feel good at the game, and then left and then had been hospitalized. But we weren't aware of any incident involving a fan at the game." Jones then pointed to the stadium’s surveillance capabilities, describing them as substantially improved from a decade or more ago. He also cited the roughly 6,000 workers on game days and said an incident escaping the team’s notice would be unusual. "We have quite a surveillance at every aspect of our game, so it is really a rare if we didn't know of any incident... We have 6,000 workers on game day," Jones said, adding his team would "of course" send any of that footage to the police department. Asked whether the Cowboys would provide footage to police if needed, Jones replied, "Of course." Meanwhile, the fan’s family is asking for help bringing their loved one home. COWBOYS GREAT MICHAEL IRVIN OUTLINES FRANCHISE'S TIMELINE TO RETAIN 'AMERICA’S TEAM' STATUS In a GoFundMe campaign titled "Bringing Mario Home to Rest," organizer Lois DeLara identified herself as Mario’s niece and said he traveled to Texas for a football game before his unexpected death. The fundraiser seeks assistance with funeral and memorial costs, transporting his remains home and expenses incurred by family members making arrangements in Texas. DeLara described the family’s struggle to grieve while facing unexpected financial obligations. The campaign does not provide a detailed account of the incident or a medical explanation for his death. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "You will forever be loved and missed," she wrote.

articles.title: Grand Slam of Darts: Michael van Gerwen beats Tom Sykes in quarter-final
articles.summary: Grand Slam of Darts: Michael van Gerwen beats Tom Sykes in quarter-final
articles.body:
Michael van Gerwen came through a stunning Grand Slam of Darts quarter-final against Tom Sykes - in which both players hit nine-dart finishes - and will play Gian van Veen in the last four.

Van Gerwen produced nine perfect darts during the opening leg in Wolverhampton, before Sykes hit back with his own in the sixth leg as he levelled the match at 3-3.

A 170 checkout from Sykes, who knocked out world number two Luke Humphries, gave him a 5-4 lead before the Englishman went 8-6 up.

But, Van Gerwen reeled off four legs in a row to go 10-8 in front and then kept up his momentum to go 14-9 ahead as he took control of the match.

The Dutchman completed a 16-11 victory with bull, averaging 105.84, hitting 14 180s and having a 50% success rate on the doubles.

"Everyone was doubting me - I'm still here, don't worry," Van Gerwen, who won the last of his three Grand Slam of Darts titles in 2017, told Sky Sports. "I'm not going away.

"Of course there are tough times, it's been hard. I've not been producing what I'm capable of but today I think I played a fantastic game."

He added: "I've never started a game with a nine-darter before in my life. That's a good thing but I also had to do it because, if you saw his scoring power in the beginning of the game, you could see he was able to do anything."

Van Gerwen will play compatriot Van Veen, who battled to a 16-14 win over Nathan Aspinall, in Sunday's semi-finals.

Van Veen raced into a 4-0 lead and, despite being pegged back to 12-12, managed to hold on and get over the line.

"Nathan and I, we always have great battles. It was always going to be a close game," said Van Veen. "It was close and I'm really happy with this win.

"I didn't score well but Nathan didn't either and he let me in. I think that's what gave me the win.

"I have to play a lot better if Michael plays like he did today."

The other last-four tie is between Wales' Gerwyn Price and Dutchman Kevin Doets.

articles.title: Why was WNBA star Jonquel Jones’ sister detained by ICE? Joe Tsai’s reported call drew attention
articles.summary: New York Liberty star Jonquel Jones faced a worrying family situation after her sister was detained by US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) while
articles.body: New York Liberty star Jonquel Jones faced a worrying family situation after her sister was detained by US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) while travelling to the United States for a ceremony honouring the basketball player. The Bahamian woman was held in Phoenix last week but was later released after a series of calls involving Liberty general manager Jonathan Kolb, team owner Joe Tsai and former Donald Trump adviser Jason Miller. She reached Washington in time to attend the retirement of Jones’ No. 35 jersey at George Washington University in Washington, DC, on November 17.How Jonquel Jones’ sister was released after Joe Tsai contacted Jason MillerJones first contacted Kolb after learning that her sister had been detained. Kolb then turned to Tsai, who reportedly contacted Miller for assistance. NetsDaily, citing a person familiar with the Liberty, reported that the intervention helped secure her release. The New York Post also reported that Jones had asked the team for help. Neither the Liberty nor Brooklyn Sports & Entertainment had immediately responded to the Post’s request for comment.The reported calls have drawn attention to Miller’s work for Brooklyn Sports & Entertainment, the company that owns the Liberty, the Brooklyn Nets and Barclays Center. NetsDaily reported that the organisation had paid Miller $1.5 million since late 2024, largely through payments of about $120,000. The Washington Post had earlier reported on his earnings and business ties. Miller is a longtime Trump ally and worked on his presidential campaigns.NetsDaily reported that Joe and Clara Wu Tsai worried a Trump administration might be difficult for the NBA and WNBA because of some players’ political views. The organisation therefore sought Miller’s advice as a preventive step. The report described the help in Jones’ sister’s case as one of several matters where Miller used his connections, but gave no details of the others.Jonquel Jones’ George Washington jersey retirement and Jorge Linares’ ICE detentionThe ceremony marked a major moment in Jones’ career. George Washington University retired her No. 35 jersey on November 17, making her the first player in the university’s women’s basketball history to receive the honour. Jones played for the university before entering the WNBA draft in 2016, when the Connecticut Sun selected her sixth overall. She joined the Liberty in 2023 and helped the team win its first WNBA championship in 2024. Jones was named Finals MVP that season. She re-signed with New York this spring and is under contract through 2028.The case comes as another athlete’s encounter with ICE has drawn attention. Former Venezuelan boxing champion Jorge Linares was detained at El Paso International Airport in Texas on Sunday, November 15, CNN reported. An ICE spokesperson described him as “a foreign national in the country without legal immigration status, arriving from Venezuela.” The agency said he entered the US on October 26, 2023, with permission for a temporary stay and “remained in the country beyond the authorized period.” CNN reported he would stay in custody “pending deportation proceedings.”Linares addressed the situation in a post on X: “I’m being held by ICE in El Paso, Texas. What a crazy situation”.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Grand Slam of Darts: Michael van Gerwen proves he is still a force to be reckoned with after reaching semi-finals
articles.summary: Debutant Kevin Doets faces three-time champion Gerwyn Price in the first semi-final before Michael van Gerwen and Gian van Veen renew their rivalry on the big stage; watch the climax of the Grand Slam of Darts in Wolverhampton live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
With Luke Littler and Luke Humphries already at home, Van Gerwen will be looking to get his hands on some TV silverware for the first time since the 2025 World Series of Darts Finals.

Van Gerwen, who threw perfection in the opening leg agains t Tom Sykes to record his first televised nine-darter on Sky Sports in 14 years , takes on Van Veen on Sunday, with debutant Kevin Doets going head-to-head with three-time champion Gerwyn Price in the first semi-final.

"There has been a lot of criticism about me in the last couple of years, and rightly so, because I wasn't performing. Then you need to make sure you pull your finger out," said Van Gerwen, who traded nine-darters with Sykes on a historic night in Wolverhampton.

"To reach the semi-final is nice, but then to also do it the way I did it today.

"This means the world to me. It has been a battle; I have to work hard, I know that, but then to also show it, it's magnificent.

"I have been feeling good, and to also produce what I am doing, I hope I can do even more later in the tournament. I am feeling good, and when I feel good, I can do anything; I know that.

"I showed some real class and some real ability, and moving on that gives me goosebumps, that gives me the energy, and I hope I can show more tomorrow."

Van Veen defeated 2022 runner-up Nathan Aspinall in a bruising battle to set up a meeting against his Dutch compatriot.

"As a Dutchman, a Grand Slam semi-final against Michael is always a dream coming true, but as you said, the way he played today, it was phenomenal," admitted the former European champion.

"If he does that on Sunday, I'm going to be in a whole lot of trouble, but hopefully he doesn't, and hopefully I'll step up my game and then it's going to be a totally different game and very close.

"Michael played phenomenal. Fair play to him, but as I said, it's going to be a totally different game on Sunday and hopefully I'll be ready.

"I will put 100 per cent focus in that semi-final and then as soon as I hopefully get that job done, then we will worry about the final.

"If you worry already about the final before the semi, you might lose quite convincingly."

'Michael's going to be feeling really good, and that's the problem for Gian'

Three-time world champion John Part speaking on Sky Sports:

"Michael has handled Gian well this year. He hasn't dropped a match to him. There's been nothing really hugely consequential about any of the matches they played.

"Michael's going to be feeling really good and that's the problem for Gian.

"He's going to have to come out, grind into the match, but he'll hopefully want to spark into the flowing, really better average stuff, the A-game type stuff.

"That was pretty good quality overall for the length of format tonight, but he'll think, ' oh, I can do so much better'. And he'll want to. And against Michael, who better to do it against."

Price will take on Doets with the Welshman into an eighth successive televised semi-final at the PDC this year, although he has yet to break his duck and is without a major victory since 2022.

'The Iceman' is chasing a fourth Grand Slam title and first in five years, but Dutchman Doets is enjoying a brilliant breakout season, claiming his first senior PDC title at Players Championship 13 in May before reaching his maiden European Tour final at the Austrian Darts Open.

He powered past Jermaine Wattimena to reach his first televised PDC semi-final, with his red-hot form impressing Wayne Mardle.

"Kevin Doets won 11 of the last 13 legs against an opponent averaging a ton. That's how good he is," said Mardle.

"I feel really strongly about Kevin Doets' future.

"It wouldn't surprise me if he deals with Gerwyn Price and goes on and wins it.

"He's playing so well so often, and you've got to play good enough often enough, and he does.

articles.title: Connor Bedard to Undergo Surgery, Latest News on Blackhawks Star's Shoulder Injury
articles.summary: Chicago Blackhawks general manager Kyle Davidson announced that captain Connor Bedard will undergo shoulder surgery, according to Ben Pope of the Chicago Sun-Times.
articles.body:
Chicago Blackhawks general manager Kyle Davidson announced that captain Connor Bedard will undergo shoulder surgery, according to Ben Pope of the Chicago Sun-Times .

The procedure will happen "this week" and a return timeline will be determined following the surgery, per Pope .

Bedard suffered the right shoulder injury during Chicago's 6-3 win over the Toronto Maple Leafs on Tuesday.

The 21-year-old has dealt with health woes as of late, previously missing 12 games due to a right shoulder injury during the 2025-26 season.

Although he didn't need surgery at the time, he eventually underwent a procedure on his left shoulder due to an injury that occurred while he was training over the offseason.

Bedard was forced to miss Chicago's first six games this season as he recovered.

He eventually returned to appear in 15 contests, recording seven goals and 11 assists.

Bedard has been a key contributor for the Blackhawks throughout his career, as the 2024 Calder Memorial Trophy winner is coming off a 2025-26 campaign in which he amassed a career-high 75 points despite being limited to 69 games played.

His latest absence is a tough blow to a Chicago squad that has only compiled a 7-14-2 record to start this season.

Anton Frondell and Frank Nazar should continue to see more playing time until Bedard is able to return, although Frondell left the Blackhawks' 4-3 win over the Calgary Flames with an injury of his own on Saturday.

articles.title: Alec Bohm accused his parents of misusing money from his baseball earnings; months later, the Phillies player's multimillion-dollar family lawsuit ended in a confidential settlement
articles.summary: Alec Bohm has spent much of his career focused on making a name for himself in Major League Baseball.
articles.body: Alec Bohm has spent much of his career focused on making a name for himself in Major League Baseball. But away from the field, the Philadelphia Phillies third baseman was dealing with a difficult situation involving the people closest to him. Bohm accused his parents of mishandling money earned through his baseball career, leading to a multimillion-dollar lawsuit. After months of legal disagreements, the two sides have now reached a settlement, although neither has disclosed the terms.The case attracted attention because it involved more than a disagreement over money. It raised questions about how Bohm's finances were managed and how a family relationship reached the point of a court battle.Why Alec Bohm Took His Parents to CourtBohm filed a lawsuit against his parents, Daniel and Lisa Bohm, seeking at least $3 million. According to his complaint, they had been handling his financial affairs since 2019 and used several limited liability companies to manage his earnings and assets.Bohm alleged that money was moved from his personal accounts into accounts belonging to these companies. He said the arrangement was supposed to help manage and invest his wealth, but claimed that some of the money was instead used for his parents' personal expenses. The complaint also raised concerns about funds connected to the Alec Bohm Foundation.The situation reportedly came to a head when Bohm asked for financial records, account statements and access to information about his holdings. He claimed that his parents provided limited information and later said they would charge him $50 an hour for managing his affairs.His parents rejected the accusations. They argued that the companies had been created with advice from Bohm's lawyer and financial adviser. They also maintained that he knew about the arrangements and had allowed them to manage his finances while he concentrated on his baseball career.From a College Baseball Prospect to a Phillies RegularBohm's career had been moving forward long before the family dispute became public. Born in Omaha, Nebraska, on August 3, 1996, he played college baseball at Wichita State University, where his performances helped him become a highly regarded prospect.The Philadelphia Phillies selected him third overall in the 2018 MLB Draft. He made his major league debut in 2020 and gradually became an important part of the team's lineup. His progress reached another milestone in 2024 when he earned his first All-Star selection.Bohm has also been involved in charitable work through the Alec Bohm Foundation. That connection became part of the legal dispute after his complaint raised questions about money associated with the organisation.Both Sides Confirm the SettlementThe legal fight continued for months, with disagreements over financial records and money held in an attorney's trust account. One issue involved $528,618 transferred into the account, which Bohm sought to have frozen while challenging related proceedings in Florida.The settlement was announced after a scheduled hearing at the Philadelphia Court of Common Pleas did not go ahead. Bohm's attorney, Gary DeVito, confirmed that an agreement had been reached but said its terms would remain confidential. His parents' attorney also confirmed the settlement and declined to comment further.The agreement brings the court battle to a close, but it leaves several questions unanswered. Neither side has explained how the financial issues were resolved or whether the settlement will help repair the family relationship.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: From practice to performance: Gagan Narang aims to bring data into India’s shooting ecosystem
articles.summary: New Delhi: In shooting, where medals can be decided by fractions, consistency is often the difference between success and failure.
articles.body: New Delhi: In shooting, where medals can be decided by fractions, consistency is often the difference between success and failure. Yet, while athletes spend hours perfecting their technique, not everyone systematically records their training or tracks their progress.That is the gap Gagan Narang hopes to address through ABHYAS (A Blueprint of Honing Your Accuracy in Shooting), a training diary designed to help shooters document their sessions, identify patterns and make their preparation more scientific.“Most Indian shooters train hard but train without a record. A shooter in a small town may fire thousands of shots a month, and a year later, neither the athlete nor the coach can say what changed, what worked and what did not. Memory is a poor coach,” Narang told TimesofIndia.com.ABHYAS allows shooters to log what they trained, the number of shots fired, scores, how they felt and observations from each session. Over time, these entries can offer a clearer picture of an athlete's development, helping coaches assess performances and provide guidance based on evidence rather than recollection.Science in sport begins with measurement, and measurement begins with the habit of writing things down. At the elite level, that habit exists, supported by data systems and support teams. At the grassroots level, it almost never does.The initiative is part of Project Amarjeet, established by Narang and Olympian and Arjuna Awardee Anuraj Singh in memory of Narang’s mother, Amarjit Narang. The launch coincided with her birth anniversary, giving the initiative a personal significance for the family.“Abhyas is a training diary built for shooters. After every session, the athlete logs what they trained, how many shots, the scores, how they felt and what they noticed. Over weeks, those entries become a picture of the athlete. A coach can look at that picture, even from another city, and give guidance based on evidence instead of a conversation at the end of a tiring day. Abhyas means practice, and the idea is simple: practice that is recorded can be improved,” he added.The emphasis is on making sports science accessible beyond the elite level, where athletes often have access to specialised teams and data systems.“Science in sport begins with measurement, and measurement begins with the habit of writing things down. At the elite level, that habit exists, supported by data systems and support teams. At the grassroots level, it almost never does. Abhyas gives a young shooter that habit for free,” Narang said.By recording their sessions, shooters can identify recurring patterns, such as scores dropping towards the end of practice or performances being affected by poor sleep. A weakness that may otherwise appear subjective can become something measurable. Coaches handling multiple athletes can also use these records to monitor individual trends, with a phone being the only requirement.Building beyond individual performancesIndia's shooting ecosystem has evolved over the past decade, with more ranges, academies, competitions, better equipment and athletes proving they can win at the highest level. Narang believes the growing acceptance of shooting as a career has also played a role.“Parents now see shooting as a real career, and that belief changes everything,” he said.However, sustaining India's progress requires attention to the grassroots rather than just its medal-winning athletes.We need coaches who keep learning. We need athletes supported in the whole of life, including the mind, the body, nutrition, studies, money and the parents who stand behind them. And we need continuity, so that a good programme does not end when a person changes jobs.“Medals at the Olympics are the visible part, but they come from thousands of young shooters training in ordinary conditions. If we look after that base, with access to pellets, coaching, guidance and information, the top will take care of itself. Progress that depends on a few brilliant individuals is fragile. Progress that depends on a strong system lasts,” Narang said.Turning individual success into sustained dominance, he believes, requires a structured pathway for athletes, continued learning among coaches and support extending beyond training.“Consistency. Individual brilliance happens when talent meets opportunity. Dominance happens when that meeting is repeated year after year, by design and not by luck. For that, we need a clear pathway from the first shot to the podium, where every athlete knows the next step. We need coaches who keep learning. We need athletes supported in the whole of life, including the mind, the body, nutrition, studies, money and the parents who stand behind them. And we need continuity, so that a good programme does not end when a person changes jobs. Too often, we rebuild from zero. The countries that dominate a sport build once and then improve every year,” he said.Better governance is not an administrative luxury. It decides how many talented young people get a real chance, so in the end, it shows up in results.Governance and the athlete's perspectiveNarang's experience as an athlete and administrator, currently the Vice President of the Indian Olympic Association (IOA) and named in the electoral college for the upcoming elections, has also shaped his views on sports governance, particularly the need for transparency, accountability and continuity in decision-making.“An athlete can accept a hard decision. What an athlete cannot accept is a decision nobody explains. Transparency means selection criteria are known in advance and followed. Accountability means those who make decisions are answerable for them. Continuity means a good policy survives a change of office bearers,” he said.He believes better governance can build confidence among athletes and parents, while also encouraging sponsors to invest in a system they trust.“Better governance is not an administrative luxury. It decides how many talented young people get a real chance, so in the end, it shows up in results,” Narang added.Abhyas may be a simple intervention, but it reflects a larger philosophy: progress in sport is not driven by talent and hard work alone. Access, structure, information and the ability to learn from every training session can be equally important.For India's shooting ambitions, the next step may not always be about firing more shots. It could be about understanding every shot better.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Player Ratings: Real Madrid 2–1 Celta Vigo
articles.summary: Jude Bellingham scored the equalizer and Carlos Espí came off the bench to win it for Real Madrid. Thibaut Courtois kept the comeback within reach, while Ard...
articles.body:
Jude Bellingham scored the equalizer and Carlos Espí came off the bench to win it for Real Madrid. Thibaut Courtois kept the comeback within reach, while Arda Güler's move into a deeper role and Vinícius Júnior's introduction helped turn the game in the second half.

Thibaut Courtois — 8. Made two outstanding saves to keep Madrid in it. The biggest came after Bernardo Silva gave the ball away with Celta already a goal up.

Ibrahima Konaté — 7.5. Recovered well from one poor giveaway. Konaté was strong in his challenges and finished with a game-high four tackles.

Dean Huijsen — 7.5. Madrid's high line looked shaky early on, and Huijsen was often the one left to cover the space behind it. He showed both strength and composure in those situations.

Trent Alexander-Arnold — 6.5. Looked sluggish early and misplaced passes he usually makes comfortably. Grew into the game, won a couple of strong defensive challenges and played some dangerous balls into the final third.

Álvaro Carreras — 6. Celta's press gave him problems. He rarely looked sure of his next pass when they closed him down on the left.

Eduardo Camavinga — 6. Lost track of his runner on Celta's goal. He won some good challenges in midfield, though, and did a better job of helping Madrid play through pressure in the second half.

Bernardo Silva — 5.5. Uncharacteristically loose on the ball. His worst giveaway handed Celta a chance to make it 2–0, and he had Courtois to thank for keeping it at one.

Arda Güler — 8. Came alive when he dropped deeper in the second half. Receiving the ball earlier in the move gave him more influence over Madrid's buildup, and he played a big part in the sequence that led to Bellingham's equalizer.

Jude Bellingham — 8.5. Defended relentlessly and still found the legs to keep crashing the box. Some of his best touches came with barely any room to move. His reward for all those runs was the equalizer, which he scored from Mbappé's pass.

Yan Diomande — 7.5. Quieter than usual, though he still looked capable of beating his man whenever Madrid found him. Carried a threat on either wing.

Kylian Mbappé — 6.5. Missed a penalty and struggled to find his range as a shooter. His most important contribution came as a provider when he picked out Bellingham for the equalizer.

Marco Cucurella — 7.5. Brought energy and fight from his first involvement. His combinations with Vinícius gave Madrid more life down the left.

Carlos Espí — 10. Five minutes, five touches, and his third match-winner of the season. What else are you supposed to give him?

Fede Valverde — 7. Ideally, he'd have had the full 90 minutes off. Mourinho needed his energy, and Valverde gave him that, even on a day when his passing was off.

Vinícius Júnior — 8. Gave Madrid a lift as soon as he came on. Combined well with Cucurella on the left and had a hand in both goals.

Endrick — 7.5. Made several good runs down the right, giving Madrid an outlet on that side while Vinícius and Cucurella combined on the other.

articles.title: Jets have chance to ‘pick’ apart interception-happy Justin Herbert
articles.summary: What happens when a team that rarely gets interceptions plays a quarterback who can’t stop throwing interceptions?
articles.body:
LOS ANGELES — What happens when a team that rarely gets interceptions plays a quarterback who can't stop throwing interceptions?

Text with Brian Costello all season as he brings Sports+ subscribers the latest Jets intel from on the field and off.

The Jets have two interceptions this season after going the entire 2025 season without one. Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert has thrown 11 interceptions this season. He has thrown at least one interception in all but one game this season; that game came last week against the Ravens, which also happened to be the Chargers' first win.

The Jets secondary grabbed their second interception of the season last week against the Bills when cornerback Azareye'h Thomas picked off Josh Allen. Could their third — or even more than one — come this week ?

The Jets have not had multiple interceptions in a game since the last game of the 2024 season.

"Anytime a quarterback is getting pressured and having to make tough throws, there's always an opportunity here," Jets safety Minkah Fitzpatrick said. "We just have to do a good job of making him uncomfortable and those opportunities will come."

While the Jets have the fewest interceptions in the NFL this season, they lead the league with 10 fumbles recovered. Getting more interceptions has been a topic of discussion all season for the Jets defense.

"I feel like every week that's definitely a focus of ours is to try to get the ball, get some takeaways," safety Dane Belton said. "Coming into games like this, that's what you've got to do to help the team. Looking back at the statistics of us this year, we're doing well on the forced fumbles but we've got to pick it up on the interceptions. Really every game, we're focused on that and if we can turn it around this week it would be awesome."

Their last win was in 2011. Their last road win was in the 2010 playoffs when the team still played in San Diego.

The Jets elevated WR Sterling Shepard for Sunday's game.

He provides some depth with Omar Cooper Jr. and Isaiah Williams both out with injuries.

TALLAHASSEE — Florida State (5-6, 3-5 ACC) lost 28-10 to NC State on homecoming at Doak Campbell Stadium. Interim head coach Rick Stockstill is now 2-1, with the Seminoles needing a win over Florida next Friday for bowl eligibility.

"After that first drive, we just weren't very good."

"We never really did stop the run. We had a hard time with stopping the run. When you can't run the ball offensively, and you can't stop the run on the other side, you give up explosive plays, it's tough sledding."

"I didn't do a good enough job having those guys ready to play."

"No, I did not. Ashton (Daniels) did some good things, did some things he'd like to have back, but it wasn't just him."

"We're down to one running back. We got exactly what we blocked for. If we blocked it for four yards, we got four yards. If we blocked it for five, we got five."

"We didn't make anybody miss. We didn't break any tackles."

"We're a very limited offense right now with the amount of injuries that we have. We're not very explosive. … When you have to methodically go four, five, six, seven yards in a clip, it's hard to do that consistently without a big play."

"He's been a little inconsistent this year, but he was special tonight. He made some really good throws, made some good throws under pressure."

"You can't make excuses, nobody cares about all that stuff, and you gotta bow your neck."

"I told them in there that they have to finish for these seniors, to finish for this football program, to finish for these Florida State fans and what this program means."

"We'll find the 11 hungry guys that are healthy and ready to go out there and compete."

"Lay your guts on the line, lay your heart, your soul on that field next Friday."

"We got to find a way to get better. We got to find a way to score more points. You're not gonna win many games scoring 10 points."

Interim head coach Rick Stockstill: NC State postgame press conference, Nov. 21

Coach Stockstill: I appreciate everybody coming out here tonight, staying through that weather and everything, so I appreciate you staying here tonight. First of all, congratulations to NC State, played a good ballgame. Disappointed in how we played. Really, offensively, after the first drive, we couldn't maintain any consistency. I bet when we look at the stats and the film, we were really bad on first down. Got behind the chains and never really established an identity on offense. We had a lot of negative plays. After that first drive we just weren't very good. Then defensively, I thought at times we were good and other times we let the quarterback, I thought he was really good tonight. He got out of the pocket, made some nice runs, and they got some explosive plays there on us in the passing game, and then we never really did stop the run. We had a hard time with stopping the run. When you can't run the ball offensively, and you can't stop the run on the other side, you give up explosive plays, it's tough sledding, and that's what it was tonight. We hurt, disappointed, we put a lot into this. I thought we had a good week of preparation and obviously I didn't do a good enough job having those guys ready to play.

Question: Rick, with the offense struggling as it did, did you consider a quarterback change at any point in those four quarters?

Coach Stockstill: No, I did not. Ashton (Daniels) did some good things, did some things he'd like to have back, but it wasn't just him. I said it in there that we're down to one running back. We got exactly what we blocked for. If we blocked it for four yards, we got four yards. If we blocked it for five, we got five. We didn't make anybody miss, we didn't break any tackles, we got exactly what we wanted. And then, we are just kind of running out of weapons a little bit. That's not to make excuses, but there's so many guys hurt right now, I thought that we got tired there in the 4th quarter because guys were having to play so many snaps. But I never thought about making a change with Ashton.

Question: With the lack of depth of the running back position, how was that felt by the offense, especially as the game wore on in the second half?

Coach Stockstill: Yeah, and you saw the first half, Ashton had to carry a little bit of a load running the ball, and obviously, Zay (Parks) had a handful of carries. We tried the jet sweeps, there with seven and eight, and we got those guys involved. We're a very limited offense right now with the amount of injuries that we have. We're not very explosive, we're not creating a lot of big plays. We did the first drive. On that first drive where we hit eight on the deep ball, but when you have to methodically go four, five, six, seven yards in a clip, it's hard to do that consistently without a big play, and we just weren't very explosive tonight.

Question: On the other side of the ball, I know Ernie (Sims) talked during the week about trying to be physical with their quarterback, get some pressure on him. It seemed like they did a pretty good job of picking up what you guys threw at them. Did they do anything especially well, or did you guys just not execute what you were trying to do?

Coach Stockstill: No, I wouldn't say that we didn't execute. I think it was probably a combination, they did a good job in pass protection and the quarterback, he broke out of there. If you can't keep him in the box, and he's a dangerous athlete getting outside. He's been a little inconsistent this year, but he was special tonight. He made some really good throws, made some good throws under pressure. To me, I think it's more you got to give them credit than it was us not doing something.

Question: They seemed to make an effort to get (Davion) Gause, the running back, the ball. I think he had 205 total yards, 134 on the ground. What were they doing to free him up in space and get him some action?

Coach Stockstill: They got a big play on the screen, on the third-down screen, they hit that, but he's a physical runner and broke tackles, ran behind his pads. They did a good job up front, their offensive line, but he's a good back, and it's like I said earlier, we never really stopped the run. And we give up that many yards to a back in the running game and they utilized him as a wildcat. They had a good plan for him. He's a good player and it wasn't anything that they did specifically for him. Most of the zone runs, and then obviously they hit him on that screen.

Question: With your limitations on offense and injuries and everything, what can you do to go back to the drawing board and change some things?

Coach Stockstill: Well, I don't know if they'll get healthy enough to play next week, but it's what you got to do. You got to hope you get a couple of guys back and we'll find that out as the week progresses. But you can't make excuses, nobody cares about all that stuff, and you gotta bow your neck. I told them in there that they have to finish for these seniors, to finish for this football program, to finish for these Florida State fans and what this program means, and don't make excuses. We all know how important that game is next week, and so we're gonna get ready for that. We'll find the 11 hungry guys that are healthy and ready to go out there and compete. We know what next week's game is all about and hopefully we get some guys back, may or may not, but we got to roll up our sleeves and go to work and come out with a great competitive mindset.

Question: On that same note, it's been a pretty emotional week for you guys, and then it's homecoming, and then you mentioned the team being hurt by the loss. How do you get the guys, with all the injuries and everything else, how do you feel like you guys can get these guys ready for Florida this quickly?

Coach Stockstill: You got to have the personal pride in yourself as a football player and the pride you have for this program. You put that helmet on with those spears on the side, it's got to mean something. And everybody hurts right now, but we got to put it behind us and come out here tomorrow, come back tomorrow, get ready to go. You can't feel sorry for yourself, and the pride that you have for this program and this football team, and the seniors and everybody involved in it, they owe it, we owe it to each other, to go out there and lay everything we got. Lay your guts on the line, lay your heart, your soul on that field next Friday night or Friday afternoon and get after it. That's the only thing I can tell you is we got to find a way to get better. We got to find a way to score more points. You're not gonna win many games scoring 10 points. To me I'm going to lean on trying to motivate them and challenge them to their competitive character, raise the intensity and get them ready to play.

articles.summary: There's a stat that shows Lane Kiffin's continued struggles against the ranked teams.
articles.body:
LSU gave Tennessee all it could handle for three quarters before the latter woke up in the final frame.

The game was tied 13-13 through three quarters before Tennessee scored the final two touchdowns to win 27-13. LSU's defense did a great job against Tennessee's passing attack, but was overwhelmed in the run game.

Vols quarterback Faizon Brandon recorded 12 carries for 112 yards and two touchdowns, and the Vols' defense only allowed seven points in the second half.

With the loss, Tigers head coach Lane Kiffin is now 6-20 in his career against top-10 teams. He's also 15-29 against ranked teams in general, per NBC's John Fanta .

This is Kiffin's first season in Baton Rouge, and despite the high expectations, the program is only 6-5 through 11 games.

Why this stat matters for Lane Kiffin's LSU tenure

Kiffin will need to do much better with this going forward, since LSU will always play some of the best teams in the country every year.

He joined LSU to turn the program around and get it over the hump, not to have seasons like this. He'll have an opportunity to turn the roster over this winter, but all that will matter is whether those changes lead to wins.

articles.title: Dave Portnoy rips Michigan fans after school upsets previously undefeated UCLA
articles.summary: After Michigan pulled off an 18-16 triple-overtime victory against No. 4 UCLA on Saturday, proud Michigan alumnus Dave Portnoy wanted no part of the celebrat...
articles.body:
After Michigan pulled off an 18-16 triple-overtime victory against No. 4 UCLA on Saturday , proud Michigan alumnus Dave Portnoy wanted no part of the celebration.

While Michigan fans were busy storming the field, Portnoy went to his camera and immediately started recording a reaction video in which he called Michigan fans "losers."

"I gotta call it as it is," Portnoy said. "I'm glad for the kids on the team, senior day. Home game, go out a winner. But we're losers."

"We're three-point underdogs against UCLA. … We're six and five. We're six and five. We're eliminated from the playoffs. Our offense is disgusting, the coach [Kyle Whittingham] is the wrong guy," Portnoy said. "I just hope this doesn't change anything, like how we're looking at this team this year, because our guy is holding a cupcake make-a-wish."

It's been a trying season for Michigan, which came into the game unranked and was on the cusp of not being bowl eligible for the first time since 2017.

"And we rush the field on UCLA, who literally, once the other kid got hurt [Ty Dieffenbach], who sucked the whole game, too. They had nothing."

Portnoy said any Michigan fans who celebrated the victory need to "get out."

"I don't give a f–k about beating UCLA when our season is over," Portnoy said.

Portnoy's Michigan rant concluded with him saying he doesn't care if Michigan beats Ohio State next week because he wants Whittingham fired.
