articles.title: ‘We don’t have a choice’: Ryan Day makes decision on defensive coordinator Matt Patricia after loss to Nebraska
articles.summary: Ohio State’s defense has been at the center of the Buckeyes’ disastrous season, and Saturday’s 31-28 loss at Nebraska may have been its worst performance yet...
articles.body:
Ohio State's defense has been at the center of the Buckeyes' disastrous season, and Saturday's 31-28 loss at Nebraska may have been its worst performance yet. Now, the spotlight is on defensive coordinator Matt Patricia, the highest-paid coordinator in college football.

After the game, head coach Ryan Day was asked whether he still had faith in Patricia. Day didn't offer a vote of confidence, but he made it clear that no changes will be made until after next week's game against Michigan, when Ohio State will "evaluate everything."

Patricia's first season as Ohio State's defensive coordinator couldn't have gone much better. The Buckeyes allowed the fewest points and yards per game of any defense in 14 years, and Ohio State rewarded him with a new three-year contract worth an average of $3.8 million per year, making him the highest-paid coordinator in college football.

But the defense lost four All-Americans from that unit, and this season has been a different story. The defense has come up short in all four of Ohio State's losses.

Ohio State blew a 23-3 fourth-quarter lead in a 24-23 loss at Texas in Week 2. The Buckeyes then gave up 30 points in a loss at USC and 41 points in a blowout home loss to Oregon, the most they'd allowed in a game since 2022. After the Oregon loss, the Buckeyes fired special teams coordinator Robby Discher , while former players called for Day to " clean house ."

On Saturday, Nebraska, which hadn't scored more than 17 points against a team with a winning record all season, put up 31. The Huskers ran for 176 yards, and Ohio State forced just two punts with zero takeaways.

With each loss, it's becoming fair to wonder whether Patricia's success last season had more to do with the elite talent on his defense than his scheme. And Ohio State didn't make him the highest-paid coordinator in the country to field a mediocre defense.

Moving on from Patricia wouldn't be cheap. Ohio State would owe him $7.7 million for the final two years of his contract, though that would be offset by his salary at a new job.

Day didn't hold back on the defense after the game.

"Disappointed. I think we're all disappointed in the outcome and, you know, we're not going to win many games if we're giving up 31 points and only getting two stops, you know, in a whole game," Day said, via HuskerOnline .

When asked what needs to change for the future of the program, Day said those decisions will have to wait.

"Well, when you watch a game like this, you got a lot of things that have to change. And, you know, I'm not going to jump anything right now, but because we have a game we got to play in another week and so like always, you know, we have to evaluate what's going on and we'll do that," Day said.

Day was then asked directly about his faith in Patricia's ability to put together a game plan for Michigan.

"Well, we don't have a choice. So, we got to get this thing together in the next week to go win this game. And that's important. You know, it's hard to be thinking about that right now coming off the field like this as disappointed and frustrated as we all are. So, you know, we got to figure it out. We got to come up with a way and then as always, at the end of the year, we'll evaluate everything and figure out, you know, what to do next," Day said.

Needless to say, it wasn't exactly a ringing endorsement. And if the defense struggles again against Michigan, Patricia may not be back for a third season.

articles.title: Kyle Whittingham explains Andrew Marsh's suspension, Ohio State status
articles.summary: Whittingham explains why Michigan suspended its leading receiver against UCLA and whether Marsh will return for The Game.
articles.body:
ANN ARBOR, Mich. -- It seemed close to impossible that Michigan football would be able to beat No. 4 UCLA at The Big House on senior day. Not only did the Bruins come in undefeated, but the languid Wolverine offense had already lost star wideout JJ Buchanan due to an injury he suffered last week at Oregon , and fellow star receiver Andrew Marsh found himself in legal trouble this week.

For an incident that occurred in February, Marsh was charged with misdemeanor indecent exposure this week. That put his status not only up in the air, but essentially demanded some semblance of punishment on the football side of things. Thus, head coach Kyle Whittingham opted to suspend Marsh for the UCLA game, and he spoke on it in the aftermath.

"Yeah, we thought that we warranted a game suspension, and Andrew agreed," Whittingham said. "I can't say much about the case, but he knew all the details and everything. It's unfortunate, and it's bad judgment, but you don't -- I don't know how to put this: It was something -- I think a one-game suspension was probably very fair to put behind this."

Photos: Michigan football celebrates Senior Day with win over UCLA

Whittingham says that, barring any new information regarding the case, Marsh is expected to return for the Ohio State game next week.

"That's the plan, to be determined," Whittingham said. "It's still an ongoing process, if new things come to light. But as we sit here tonight, I would expect that he'd be back next week."

As far as the offense was concerned, it did about as well as it could without its top two wide receivers on the field and against the nation's No. 4 defense -- the toughest played thus far. Bryce Underwood returned as the starting quarterback and he wasn't exactly efficient. But he found several pass catchers he hadn't thrown to with regularity earlier in the year.

Six players caught passes in Marsh's absence, with freshmen tight end Mason Bonner, wide receivers Travis Johnson, Salesi Moa, and running back Savion Hiter combining for nine catches for 101 yards. Bonner caught one of the Wolverines ' two touchdowns.

Whittingham said there wasn't a ton of changes to the game plan without Marsh, and he's excited about the future of the young talent making plays.

"Well, it changed it a little bit, not a ton," Whittingham said. "We didn't completely scrap the throw game, obviously. And Travis Johnson's got a big upside as well in this program. All those guys I mentioned, those five freshmen that played so much tonight, are going to be major contributors in the very near future. And so we just tailored things to their skill set.

"But we didn't shy away from throwing football. The tight ends stepped up, like you said, and contributed as well. So we didn't throw it a ton. We haven't thrown it a ton this year. We've thrown the ball like 20, 25, maybe 30 times."

Up next, Michigan football will travel to Ohio State to face the Buckeyes for the final regular season of the year.

articles.title: No. 5 Texas avoids letdown, routs Arkansas 45-3 on Senior Day
articles.summary: Arch Manning accounted for three touchdowns and Jelani McDonald recorded a pick-six as the Longhorns extended their winning streak to a season-high five game...
articles.body:
AUSTIN (KXAN) — There were no signs of what Texas head coach Steve Sarkisian calls "relief syndrome" on Senior Day at Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium, as the No. 5 Longhorns cruised to a 45-3 victory over Arkansas.

Texas jumped out to a 14-0 lead just six minutes into the game and never looked back.

"I was really proud of the team," Sarkisian said. "We challenged them on Monday up until last night, this is an opportunity to really show the growth of the team, the maturity of the team from where we were at the beginning of the season to where we are today. Having such an emotional game late last Saturday night, and then to turn around and get ourselves prepared to play, and to play at a high level at all three phases, and I thought the guys did that."

Manning leads efficient offensive performance

The Longhorns capitalized on excellent field position on their opening possession, putting together an efficient 7-play, 52-yard drive capped by a 3-yard Arch Manning rushing touchdown. It was the first of three offensive touchdowns for Texas in the first half, all accounted for by Manning.

On Arkansas' ensuing possession, the Texas defense did what it has done all season — create turnovers. Jelani McDonald was in the right place at the right time, returning an interception for a touchdown to double the Longhorns' lead.

The pick-six marked McDonald's fourth interception in the past two games, following his three-interception performance against LSU.

Manning and the Texas offense kept their foot on the gas in the second quarter, with the quarterback tossing touchdown passes to Emaree Winston and Emmett Mosley V to help the Longhorns build a commanding 31-3 halftime lead.

Slow starts to the second half have been an area of concern for Texas throughout the season, but that wasn't the case Saturday. The Longhorns marched 75 yards in 10 plays on their opening possession of the second half, capped by a 1-yard Michael Terry III rushing touchdown.

With Texas leading 38-3 heading into the fourth quarter, Manning's day was done. The quarterback completed 21 of 25 passes for 287 yards and accounted for three total touchdowns in what could be his final regular-season home game at DKR.

"First of all, I thought Arch (Manning) had a heck of a game," Sarkisian said. "I thought he used his legs in a timely manner. Obviously, had the called quarterback run for a touchdown, had another called quarterback run on a third down to convert. Thought he used his legs to scramble to get completions, but then I also thought he showed good poise in the pocket."

Freshman running back Derrek Cooper rounded out the scoring for Texas with a 4-yard rushing touchdown midway through the fourth quarter.

Will Muschamp's defensive unit remained stout against an Arkansas rushing attack that had eclipsed 150 yards on the ground against four SEC opponents this season.

The Longhorns limited the Razorbacks to 110 rushing yards.

In addition to generating points of its own with McDonald's pick-six, the Texas defense limited Arkansas to just two trips inside the red zone and surrendered only three points.

The Longhorns also got a glimpse into the future of their secondary, as five-star freshman John Meredith III recorded his first career interception in the closing minutes of the fourth quarter.

A Senior Day to remember, with more to play for

For the 38 seniors honored before Saturday's kickoff, the Longhorns delivered exactly what Sarkisian wanted — a win in their final regular-season home game at DKR.

"I'm really happy that our seniors got to have this as their final game experience in [Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium]," Sarkisian said. "... You think about a lot of those guys who have given their blood, sweat and tears to this program for three, four, five years, to have this be their lasting memory at DKR, their final home game. That's a really cool moment for them and appreciate all that they have done for the program and continue to do as we forge forward in the season."

With a dominant win over unranked Arkansas, Texas extended its winning streak to a season-high five games, avoiding the type of letdown it experienced earlier this season when the Longhorns dropped back-to-back games to unranked Oklahoma and Florida.

With one game remaining in the regular season, the Longhorns have built a strong case for a top-four spot in the College Football Playoff rankings, boasting a 9-2 overall record that includes five wins over AP Top 25 opponents.

Texas now turns its attention to another longtime rival, traveling to College Station to face Texas A&M at Kyle Field in the regular-season finale.

Kickoff is set for 6:30 p.m. Friday, Nov. 27.

Below are live updates from Texas' win against Arkansas .

5:39 p.m. — INTERCEPTION TEXAS: Five-star freshman John Meredith III records his first career interception, giving the Longhorns their second takeaway of the afternoon. Texas leads Arkansas 45-3 with 2:32 remaining in the fourth quarter.

articles.title: ‘We have to stick together’ — Vincent Kompany confident amid Bayern Munich crisis
articles.summary: The FC Bayern manager wants to focus on the basics to ride past the major injury setbacks.
articles.body:
Bayern Munich just went from the frying pan straight into the fire. The Bundesliga fixture against 1. FC Köln added to the existing injury woes of the German giants. Ballon d'Or winner Harry Kane and Michael Olise have both picked up knocks with Kane estimated to sit out for at least a couple of months. To further rub salt in the wounds, the 1-1 draw has also opened up the league's first place for grabs if Borussia Dortmund can win on Saturday.

"We have to stick together 100%. Even when things get difficult and unpleasant, we have to embrace it this time. We simply need to make sure we pick up our points. We also have to see this as an opportunity for new players to come into the team, players we perhaps don't know that well yet, but who could become important for us again. That could turn into a strength later in the season. That's the only way we can look at it. Everything else right now… it is what it is," said Kompany(as captured by @iMiaSanMia ) in a strong message to tackle the uncertain period ahead.

As it currently stands only Lennart Karl and Jamal Musiala remain the only attackers with senior team experience available for Bayern, though Olise is expected to make a quick recovery. Left-back Nathaniel Brown and youth players from the academy will be relied on to attempt to immediately bridge the massive gaps due to the injuries. Although it has to be said that this will be a mountain of responsibility on the young shoulders of the academy players.

articles.title: Michigan upsets No. 4 UCLA 18-16 in triple overtime, ending Bruins' unbeaten season
articles.summary: All UCLA had to do was defeat Michigan in The Big House.Instead, the No. 4 Bruins walked off the turf in defeat for the first time this season, falling to th...
articles.body:
ANN ARBOR, Mich. — UCLA traveled to Ann Arbor searching for a historic win.

A victory would secure the program's first 11-win season, tie the school mark for single-season conference victories and clinch a berth in the Big Ten championship game.

All UCLA had to do was defeat Michigan in The Big House.

Instead, the fourth-ranked Bruins walked off the turf in defeat for the first time this season, falling to the Wolverines 18-16 in triple overtime on Saturday at Michigan Stadium.

"This was a battle, and obviously we came up a little bit short," head coach Bob Chesney said postgame. "We have to find a way to get better, period."

After marching down the field on a 15-play, 77-yard drive to tie the game with 10 seconds remaining on a jump-pass touchdown from Anthony Woods to Brayden Loftin, UCLA headed to overtime deadlocked at 10, looking to add another chapter to a remarkable campaign.

What followed was a nightmare — one that cost the Bruins their undefeated season, a guaranteed trip to Indianapolis and maybe worst of all — their quarterback.

On the opening snap of overtime, senior quarterback Ty Dieffenbach rushed to his right and was brought down at the 19-yard line by Michigan defender Troy Bowles for a gain of six yards.

Dieffenbach remained down on the play, appearing in serious pain before being carted off the field.

Nov 21, 2026; Ann Arbor, Michigan, USA; UCLA quarterback Ty Dieffenbach (14) reacts after an injury in overtime at Michigan Stadium.

Backup Madden Iamaleava took over under center and struggled to move the ball against a standout Michigan defense, failing to complete a pass while hesitating on multiple scrambles in crucial moments.

The most glaring miscue came on third-and-6 from the Michigan 21-yard line, when Iamaleava stepped up in the pocket with a wide-open lane to move the chains. The sophomore failed to capitalize on the defensive breakdown and was tripped up short of the first-down marker.

Both teams traded field goals in the first two overtimes, setting up a sudden-death battle of two-point conversion plays tied at 16.

The Bruins came up empty on their two-point attempt, with Iamaleava unable to get a pass away after spinning to his left.

One play later, Michigan quarterback Bryce Underwood delivered the decisive blow, rolling to his right and finding Jalen Hoffman in the end zone for the game-winner, handing UCLA its first defeat and sending Michigan fans storming onto the field in celebration.

The stunning loss snapped a 10-game winning streak for UCLA and halted a 20-game regular-season winning streak for Chesney.

UCLA could not generate sustained momentum on offense throughout the game, producing season lows in total yards (296 on 74 plays, or 4.0 per play), points (16) and rushing yards (107).

The Bruins also struggled to protect the ball with Dieffenbach committing three turnovers, throwing an interception and losing two fumbles — one of which gave Michigan a short field and set up a go-ahead score early in the fourth quarter. The Cal Poly transfer completed 19 of 30 passes for 188 yards before exiting with the lower-body injury.

"We just have to clean up the mistakes," senior running back Wayne Knight said after the game. "We can't turn the ball over."

Knight, the Bruins' most productive offensive weapon with a team-high 15 touchdowns this season, was unable to produce on the ground against Michigan's defensive line, rushing for 30 yards on 11 carries. The fifth-year back led the team with six catches for 38 yards.

"It was hard to run the ball," Chesney said. "We just weren't able to convert on it."

UCLA's opportunistic defense, which entered the day leading the nation with 30 takeaways, did everything it could to keep the Bruins in contention despite the stagnant offensive attack. Defensive end Aiden Gobaira provided the lone turnover with a strip-sack at the end of the first half to set up a field goal.

The loss undoubtedly stings with a shot to clinch a spot in the Big Ten title game slipping away, yet the uncertainty surrounding Dieffenbach's health looms even larger — setting up a scenario where a defeat next week to USC could leave the Bruins on the outside looking in.

A campaign defined by highs hit its first real low, and the fallout could drastically alter UCLA's College Football Playoff hopes.

With the Trojans on deck next week at the Rose Bowl to close out the regular season, UCLA's postseason fate could now rest in the hands of its third-string quarterback.

articles.title: Week 11 Preview: #1 Seed on the Line?
articles.summary: It very well could be.
articles.body:
The Minnesota Vikings will travel to Mexico City to face the 8-1 San Francisco 49ers in a game that could very well determine the #1 seed in the NFC playoff bracket in January.

With the Vikings currently tied with the 7-2 Detroit Lions and Chicago Bears in the ridiculously good NFC North, a win over the 49ers could put them in the driver's seat for the rest of the way. After Sunday, the schedule gets much easier, with five of the final seven games at U.S. Bank Stadium. The Vikings also have the benefit of already being 3-1 in the division, with the final two at home. The Lions and Bears each have four division games left. And while the Packers may "just" be 6-4 and destined for last place, they're certainly no pushovers.

A loss to the 49ers certainly wouldn't dash the good guys' hopes for a division crown, as they'd still control their own destiny; it could, for all intents and purposes, slam the door on the coveted #1 seed in the NFC and its lone bye. The 49ers do have some tricky games left, but I'd think the only one they'd be underdogs in would be the Week 16 road game against the Kansas City Chiefs. At effectively two games behind, the Vikings would probably need to be flawless.

Kirk Cousins' return changes the formula dramatically. If the trade didn't happen, I'd give the Vikings offense little to no shot at hitting 20+ points here. Or maybe even 10. And this is with the knowledge that the 49ers defense is kind of living off its reputation a bit from the earlier Kyle Shanahan era.

Don't get me wrong, they're solid. But it's not the unit from the 2019-2022 Robert Saleh-DeMeco Ryans years. That said, new (and highly experienced) coordinator Raheem Morris has them playing well: 11 th in points per game (21.8), 6 th in total yards (308), 17 th in pass yards allowed (226), 2 nd in rush yards allowed (82.6), and 20 th in 3 rd -down conversion rate (41%).

The standout stat is their exceptional success so far at stopping the run. The Vikings average 108.6 per game (19th) but improved in both volume and efficiency last week with Cousins back – e.g., higher YPC (4.2) and seven rushing first downs. Avoiding 3rd-and-long situations will be crucial in this one. Nice gains on 1st and 2nd downs will also open up the play-action game, which I'm sure will be a focus for Kevin O'Connell. Keeping the 49ers defense on their toes will make an already average pass defense even less effective.

Many 49ers sites are focusing on the fact that Cousins already faced this defense a few weeks ago, and the results were…suboptimal: 216 yards, 1 TD, 3 INTs, and a 55.3 QBR. Does this matter? To a certain extent, I suppose. Does it mean history will repeat itself? Definitely not. Different play-caller, better offensive personnel, and almost certainly a more effective game plan, with that game on film to learn from. To be honest, I fully expect this to be a far more challenging unit to face than the Packers were a week prior.

If you're going to go there, it's only fair to point out that Cousins is 2-1 in regular-season games in a Vikings uniform against Shanahan's 49ers, averaging 286.7 yards passing in those games, with 6 TDs and 2 INTs for an overall passer rating of 99.4. One of those was a great home win in 2023, when he passed for 378 yards in a victory without Justin Jefferson against the then 5-2 49ers.

Again, all that aside, getting the running game going early in this one will be critical. Allowing Nick Bosa, Keion White, and company to go wild repeatedly on 3rd-and-long isn't ideal, even if the 49ers' overall pass-rush metrics (e.g., sack rate) this season have been at or below average.

Again, this is your main event of the evening. Strength vs. strength. The NFL's #1 scoring/EPA defense faces the #1 yardage/efficiency offense. We all know how historically dominant the Vikings' defense has been. I touched on it a few days ago. But with apologies to the Bills, Lions, and Bears, this will almost certainly be the season's biggest challenge.

The 49ers are formidable: 2nd in points per game (31.2), 1st in total yards (399.8), 7th in pass yards (255.8), 3rd in rush yards (144), and 1st in 3rd-down conversion rate (52%). The Vikings' rankings in those categories? 1st, 2nd, 2nd, 17th, and 3rd, respectively.

The number that stands out to Vikings fans is that we're 17th in rushing yards allowed per game. There are vulnerabilities, no doubt. This is especially true since it's no secret that Christian McCaffrey is the straw that stirs the drink for the 49ers offense. He's Brock Purdy's security blanket and among the most dangerous dual threats in the NFL. But digging a bit deeper into the numbers, I found that the Vikings are much better (7th) in run EPA/play, at around -0.10. That makes you feel a bit better, but the eye test (for me, anyway) shows the concerns are legitimate.

If the Vikings are effective at stopping the run on early downs, it will play right into our hands. What's unique about Flores' scheme is that it flips traditional schematic reasoning on its head. Logic would dictate that the more aggressive the defense, the more vulnerable a team becomes in the quick, on-time passing game. Instead, the Vikings did a good job of taking that away in the last matchup against Purdy and the 49ers in 2024. ESPN's Jason McCourty and Dan Orlovsky had a great discussion about it that's worth your time.

And here's another post from The Athletic's Alec Lewis that's just ridiculous.

In the end, Kyle Shanahan is 0-5 when Brian Flores is on the opposing sideline, whether as a head coach or a coordinator. 49ers fans will say he's due. It's only a matter of time. Vikings fans will counter that this is the best Flores unit Shanahan has ever faced. Who will be right? We shall see.

The unique wildcard here is the altitude issue in Mexico City and which team's differing methods will prove more effective. I'm not a biologist and have no clue which strategy is better. I'm sure there's science supporting both approaches; why would a team deliberately put itself at such a disadvantage?

What I do know is that after Week 1, the 49ers had the oldest average roster in the NFL (27.49 years). They've since traded for 34-year-old Keenan Allen and 32-year-old DeForest Buckner to play prominent roles. The Vikings have similar issues, specifically with Harrison Smith (37) and Kyle Van Noy (35). You can also note Kirk Cousins (38). But there's a fundamental difference between a quarterback taking three- and five-step drops and a receiver running routes and blocking all game. The same goes for an interior lineman battling in the trenches for four quarters. Depth and scheme comfort/familiarity on both sides of the ball will be important here. Expect more varied snap counts than usual after this one.

I'm cautiously optimistic about this game. Jordan Addison being out again isn't ideal, but it opens opportunities for a Jauan Jennings revenge game, and Myles Price and Tai Felton played well last week, too. The key for Cousins will be to avoid turnovers, and the way to do that is not to press, which I felt was a bit of an issue on his return last week. The interception that counted was one example, and the one that didn't, because his knee was fortunately down, was another. If he takes what's there, nothing more and nothing less, the Vikings offense will be fine. The name of the game is to keep the chains moving and to afford the defense time to recover. Unless there's an unexpected turnover barrage, whoever wins time of possession is likely the victor. That's always true, but it's even more critical given the atmospheric conditions.

On defense, it all comes down to scheming effective pressure on Purdy without committing more than five too often. Listen, Flores is going to bring the heat, but it wouldn't shock me if the blitz rate were slightly reduced from the record-breaking highs if it's not getting home early. Purdy isn't going to be easily rattled and, with time, will quickly make the proper reads to exploit the mid-15 to 20-yard range, where we can sometimes be susceptible. And, of course, having to account for McCaffrey, who can take it to the house from anywhere, on every play could even out the numbers game.

I've got a death grip on the positive vibes since Cousins' return, and I have no plans to let go until the situation warrants it. I want that bye week, and I think we'll stay on track to get it.

articles.title: Does Tarik Skubal Dictate Whether the Dodgers Have a Successful Offseason?
articles.summary: Dodgers Nation's Doug McKain says the Los Angeles Dodgers' offseason is a failure if they don't sign left-handed starter Tarik Skubal.
articles.body:
Free agent starting pitcher Tarik Skubal is the best player on the market this offseason, and the Dodgers—as they tend to do with the best of the best—are keeping tabs on the left-hander.

That being said, they aren't the only ones. The Toronto Blue Jays, New York Mets and San Diego Padres all held meetings with the starter as well, and Dodgers Nation's Doug McKain believes the Dodgers' offseason would be a failure if they don't retain the two-time Cy Young winner.

Skubal spent the last couple of months of the season with the Dodgers after LA traded for him at Aug. 3's deadline, and while he wasn't at his best during his time with the Dodgers, he still had a 2.61 ERA with 70 strikeouts in 62 innings pitched.

"I do think this would be a failed offseason if they're considering going long-term on Tarik Skubal, and now you're throwing out dollar figures, and then he goes with the Mets because he wants to get the top dollar," McKain said . "Even though their preference may be a shorter-term AAV deal, you're not getting that with a prime pitcher. Stop. Don't even think about it. It doesn't make sense. Especially because pitchers deal with injuries.

"Skubal wants a long-term pact, anywhere from seven to 10 years. If you look at the Mets, Steve Cohen is reportedly 'all-in'. The Mets are the favorite. The Mets and Steve Cohen met with Skubal before the Dodgers did."

Are the Mets the Favorite to Land Skubal?

As McKain said, the Mets met with Skubal before any other team, and reportedly already offered him a nine-year, $390 million deal Friday.

That figure shatters the previous record contract for a pitcher, previously held by Yoshinobu Yamamoto with his 10-year, $325 million deal.

Skubal clearly wants a long-term contract rather than the short-term, high-AAV contracts the Dodgers gave out last season to Kyle Tucker and Edwin Diaz, meaning they'll have to change how they normally do things to retain Skubal.

But per the New York Post's Jon Heyman, they could go against the status quo and do so.

"The Dodgers also have told folks there are circumstances whereby they'd still do longer deals, and they did them for Mookie Betts, Yoshinobu Yamamoto and Shohei Ohtani in the past," Heyman wrote.

"To be a serious player, they'd almost have to go long considering the game's best pitcher is extremely unlikely to have to settle for a short deal."

With the race for Skubal heating up and less than two weeks before a potential lockout, the Dodgers will have to move quickly to ensure they don't miss out on the southpaw.

articles.title: 'Baltimore isn't a talking point to me': Carmelo Anthony calls out Marlon Humphrey
articles.summary: Baltimore Ravens cornerback Marlon Humphrey made the wrong kind of headlines this past week after making a joke on his podcast at the expense of the city he...
articles.body:
Baltimore Ravens cornerback Marlon Humphrey made the wrong kind of headlines this past week after making a joke on his podcast at the expense of the city he represents on the field.

During an episode of his podcast, The Marlon Humphrey Show , Humphrey was asked what Baltimore was best at making, and responded, "criminals," with a laugh. Given that Humphrey has played for the Ravens for a decade, the remark quickly made the rounds as fans and media alike expressed their disappointment.

Humphrey has since apologized, but was sent home for the week by the team and will be inactive for Sunday's game against the Carolina Panthers as a punishment for the comments. He has also been on the receiving end of critiques from the likes of Shannon Sharpe and Kevin Wildes , who suggested maybe it was time for him to stop podcasting.

On Friday, former NBA star and current analyst Carmelo Anthony joined the voices of those calling out Humphrey. Anthony, who played his high school basketball in the Baltimore area, sent a clear message to Humphrey via a series of posts to his Instagram account.

"Listen. I've been sitting with this one for a couple of days, because Baltimore isn't a talking point to me. It's my blood," Anthony wrote. "I came up on Myrtle Avenue in West Baltimore. I saw what this city can take from you. I lost friends to the streets, and I watched people I loved get swallowed by a system that was built to swallow them. I know the reputation. I've heard every joke and every headline my whole life.

"So when one of our own stands on our name and says the best thing Baltimore makes is criminals, and then laughs that it'll get cut out, that doesn't get cut out for me. It doesn't get cut out for the kid in Baltimore who heard it. It doesn't get cut out for the mother working two jobs to keep her son off the corner. And it doesn't get cut out for the man who did his time, came home, and is fighting every day to be seen as more than his worst moment."

Anthony acknowledged Humphrey's apology, but challenged him to get more involved in the local community and engage with the city and its people.

"You don't get to rep Baltimore on Sunday and talk about it like an outsider on Wednesday," he wrote.

Anthony closed out his message by asking that Humphrey make good on an invitation that Baltimore mayor Brandon Scott made to him to meet with residents who are working to make the city a better place and keep others from making the mistakes of their past.

"The Mayor opened a door. Walk through it," Anthony wrote. "And when you do, call me. I'll meet you there. Let's sit with these young boys together and let them hear from two men who wear this city that they are not what anybody says they are."

Humphrey clearly didn't realize the impact his words would have when he made his comments. While he is serving the punishment that his team gave him this week, it could go a long way in mending some of the bridges he might have burned if he took up Anthony on his offer.

articles.summary: Penn State football suffered a stunning 25 to 24 loss to Rutgers. Here is the postgame report card for the team.
articles.body:
You can't quite write this script anymore for this team. After seemingly looking like they would pull out a win, Rutgers pulled off a gutsy 2-point conversion to steal a 25-24 . Overall, it wasn't as if the Nittany Lions played too poorly, it was just a game of chaos that the Scarlet Knights pulled out in the end. This one will be looked at long and hard in Happy Valley long after this season is over.

Here is a look at the postgame report card for the Nittany Lions against Rutgers.

His stats may never be pretty, but Rocco Becht sure knows how to weather a storm. His experience in situations such as these proves that the journey to get to this point was worth it. His final stat-line (14/20 for 232 yards and a touchdown and 20 rushing yards and a touchdown) don't jump off the page but that productivity is what makes his progression through this season fun to watch. At the end of the day, when fans look back at this season, there was a lot left on the field by Becht, including in games such as this. But you can't say college football's winningest football player didn't leave it all out there. It sucks that he won't end his home career with the squad with a win, but tonight was almost certainly not his fault.

Without Carson Hansen and James Peoples after a couple of drives, it's safe to say the run game reverted back to its early-season ineptitude. After Cam Wallace' s first-quarter touchdown, it was very much a slog on the ground for the Nittany Lions. Still, Wallace did have 95 yards and was perhaps the offense's most consistent weapon outside of Sowell. Still, no one outside of him was able to fill the void. As a result, the run game stagnated in the second half, only generating 38 rushing yards. The only good thing about this unit is that it could look wholly different come next year.

It's truly a shame that Chase Sowell was basically a one-year rental for the Nittany Lions. Without him, who knows where the explosive element from this offense would have come from this season? Without their potential breakout star Koby Howard, Chase Sowell has led the way at the position, and this game was no different. He led the way for the unit with 122 yards and a touchdown, providing just enough offensive spark when it was needed. Still, when your second leading receiver only has 54 yards, you eventually have to find a certain balance. It's nice to rely on a superstar athlete, but not all the time. This is something Matt Campell will have to address in the long term.

This defense was ultimately the big let down on the day, and blame will be placed squarely on their shoulders. Against a QB with cracked ribs, the fact that the Rutgers offense scored 25 points and secured the win has to be a little unnerving. Tony Rojas again had to be the emotional leader of the unit, and they even recorded a safety. Still, big plays will always be overshadowed by long drives. Ultimately, the Nittany Lions gave up too many of them. Add in Antwan Raymond having 2 TDs on the ground, and all their issues were laid bare. There will be questions about why they sometimes have weird lapses and lulls in the middle and the end of games, especially after this latest debacle. If they're not answered, it will be an indictment of a unit that could have been much better.

The special teams were nothing to write home about. Nathan Tiyce was busier than usual, punting four times for 161 yards, averaging 1 per punt. No field goals were required either, although it's interesting to note that Cristiano Rosa was the kicker for tonight. The biggest disappointment was perhaps the play of Zay Robinson. Ultimately, this unit is failed by the overall ineptitude of the team around them.

While this game wasn't necessarily about coaching, it's the fact that it became too chaotic that should worry Penn State fans. This was a 2-8 Rutgers team that was able to pull out a gutsy victory. While these games each year always seem to be crazy, this year's iteration should have been easy for what was seemingly a rejuvenated squad. Campbell will have to eventually figure out what goes wrong with this team in the second half of these games, or else his tenure will have a lot more painful losses like this one.

What can you say when you lose in such inexplicable fashion when you had a win in your grasp? Eventually, chaos catches up to you and Penn State simply could not handle it. This has been too much of a common theme all year long and it's not entirely on the players, but the coaching staff as well. Sure, there will be excuses, but they are not good enough for this talented a roster.

The Penn State Nittany Lions will take on the Maryland Terrapins on the road at Byrd Stadium to close out their regular season. Kickoff is scheduled for 3:30 PM ET.

articles.title: NFC North continues its historic dominance
articles.summary: They're 27-10 overall, and 21-4 in games outside the division.
articles.body:
The NFC North continues to perform like no other division in the league.

Three of the teams (Lions, Bears, Vikings) have a record of 7-2 through 10 weeks. The Packers are 6-4.

The combined record of 27-10 equates to a success rate of 73 percent — the highest by any division through Week 10 in NFL history.

Outside the division, the teams of the NFC North are 21-4. The 84-percent success rate is the most for any division through Week 10 since the AFL-NFL merger.

This weekend, the Lions host the Bucs, the Bears host the Saints, and the Vikings face the 49ers in Mexico City.

In theory, all four teams could make the playoffs. That would require the fourth-place team landing higher in the standings than the second-place team in each of the other three divisions.

And that makes Wednesday night's game between the 6-4 Packers and 6-4 Rams critical to the outcome of the chase for the wild-card berths in the NFC.

articles.title: Tyreek Hill’s Health Update Sparks Chiefs Interest
articles.summary: Tyreek Hill's agent gives a bleak update on the star receiver's knee. See why the Kansas City Chiefs are now the favorite to sign him if he gets healthy.
articles.body:
Former Miami Dolphins star Tyreek Hill is not ready to play yet. His agent, Drew Rosenhaus, told Dianna Russini that Hill has not been cleared for football. Rosenhaus said, "He's not been cleared yet. He is still working to get back to 100%. He's still working to get to a point where he'll be cleared to play football." The wide receiver suffered a dislocated knee and torn ligaments in a game against the New York Jets last year. Since that injury, the Dolphins cut him, and he has not signed with a new team.

The Kansas City Chiefs are now seen as the most likely landing spot for Hill if he returns. Reports suggest his odds favor the former champions because they need an explosive playmaker. Hill missed the rest of the 2025 season after his injury. Last season with Miami, he played in just four games. He caught 21 passes for 265 yards and one touchdown before going down. His health remains the only thing stopping him from joining a contender.

Rosenhaus emphasized that the focus is on getting Hill to full strength. The agent added, according to Yahoo Sports , "I think the focus is on his health and getting back to 100%. He has just done a beautiful job and he's doing awesome." Hill traveled to Germany to work with Usain Bolt's doctor. He has tried many different methods to heal his knee. Rosenhaus praised the effort, noting, "I have to take my hat off to Tyreek. I mean, he had a tough injury, to put it mildly, and a very challenging rehab." There is no set date for his return because the team wants to avoid rushing him back.

Some experts believe Hill could be the missing piece for a top offense. Andrew Buller-Russ wrote for Sportsnaut that Seattle or Kansas City might take a chance on him. The Seahawks have Jaxon Smith-Njigba, but the drop-off after him is big. Adding Hill would make life easier for any quarterback who can throw deep. The Chiefs need help slowing down their own opponents, but they also need a weapon to score. Hill fits that role perfectly if his legs come back.

While Hill waits for clearance, the Dolphins are fighting for a top draft pick. ESPN's latest projections show Miami has a 40 percent chance to get the number one overall pick. With a 38 percent chance, the Tennessee Titans sit right behind them. This race is so tight that a single loss could change the order. Among fans, a strange mood has arisen from the pressure to lose. A satirical piece depicted a fan named "Zane Gonzalez" watching the Jets win the Super Bowl as his team hunts for a playoff victory. In his parents' basement, Gonzalez sits and queries his stuffed dolphin, according to Yahoo Sports , "Where did we go wrong, T.D?" He blames a specific loss to the Colts that knocked Miami out of the running for the top pick. "You're right, it was that 2027 draft. That win over the Colts knocked us out of the running for the top pick in the draft!" Gonzalez even dreams of using time travel to fix the mistake.

The Dolphins face the Buffalo Bills on Sunday, Nov. 22, at 1 p.m. ET in a game that could impact their draft standing.

articles.title: 'What a play!': Rutgers stuns Penn State on last-second touchdown
articles.summary: Rutgers snapped a 17-game losing streak against Penn State with a last-second touchdown and 2-point conversion. See how the Scarlet Knights did it
articles.body:
In a season that once seemed lost, Penn State football found new life, winning three consecutive games after a disastrous 3-4 start under first-year head coach Matt Campbell .

That positive momentum ended this weekend, though — and in about the most heartbreaking way imaginable.

Trailing the Nittany Lions by seven, 24-17, with a first-and-goal from the Penn State 3-yard line and six seconds remaining in the fourth quarter, Rutgers quarterback AJ Surace tossed a screen to star running back Antwan Raymond, who caught the pass at the 6. He was swarmed by Nittany Lions defenders and juked one before being wrapped up at the 3. Before he could be brought down, though, Raymond tossed the ball behind him to teammate Ben Black III, who gathered the ball and got into the end zone with no time remaining.

Rather than kick the extra point and send the game into overtime, Scarlet Knights coach Greg Schiano went for the win, going for the ensuing 2-point conversion. His team paid off his bold call, with Surace connecting with a wide-open Clay Thevenin in the flat for the score, handing Rutgers a thrilling 25-24 victory.

It was an improbable win in more ways than one for the Scarlet Knights.

Rutgers' win snapped a 17-game losing streak against the Nittany Lions and was its first win over Penn State since 1988. The Scarlet Knights entered the game with just a 2-8 record this season, with five of those eight losses coming by at least 16 points, including a 37-21 home loss in their season-opener against UMass. As a 24-point underdog, they fell behind, 16-0, with five minutes remaining in the second quarter and were down 14, 24-10, with 11 minutes remaining in the fourth quarter.

From there, an offense that had scored just 10 combined points in its past two games scored 15 points in the final 10:14 — including a touchdown its fans won't soon forget.

articles.title: No. 5 Duke pulls away from Columbia 71-47 behind Emilee Skinner's 17 points
articles.summary: NEW YORK (AP) — Emilee Skinner scored 17 points and Toby Fournier added 15 to help No. 5 Duke beat Columbia 71-47 on Saturday night.
articles.body:
NEW YORK (AP) — Emilee Skinner scored 17 points and Toby Fournier added 15 to help No. 5 Duke beat Columbia 71-47 on Saturday night.

Duke (6-0) led by two at the half before outscoring Columbia 23-14 in the third quarter led by Skinner and Fournier. The third-team AP All-American had a quiet first half with only three points before scoring six quick ones in the third quarter to help the Blue Devils extend their advantage to double digits.

Columbia (3-3) was only able to get within eight the rest of the game as Duke scored nine of the first 11 points in the fourth quarter to blow the game open.

The Blue Devils have a tough schedule coming up with five of their next six games against the top 10, including No. 7 UConn and No. 1 South Carolina.

This game closed out a difficult three-game stretch for Columbia, which also hosted No. 2 Michigan and played at then-No. 19 Maryland. It's been 12 years since a mid-major program has played three consecutive regular-season games against ranked teams, including two top-five opponents, according to STATS Perform. New Mexico did it in 2014, although two of those games were on neutral courts.

Columbia jumped out on Duke building a seven-point lead in the second quarter before the Blue Devils rallied to take a 30-28 lead at the break. Thomas' jumper on the baseline with 56 seconds left gave Duke its first lead of the game and was the last score of the half.

Fliss Henderson had nine points in the first half, making all three of her shots as the Lions shot 61% from the field in the opening 20 minutes against one of the best defensive teams in the country. Columbia couldn't maintain that hot shooting in the second half as Duke dictated on the defensive end holding the Lions to just 22% (6 for 27) in the second half.

Henderson and Riley Weiss each had 12 for Columbia.

Duke: Plays No. 7 UConn in Boston on Nov. 28.

Columbia: Plays Stanford to begin a three-game tournament in Hawaii on Nov. 27.

articles.title: Struble and Marchessault lead the Predators to a 4-3 win over the Penguins
articles.summary: (AP) — Jayden Struble and Jonathan Marchessault each had a goal and an assist to lead the Nashville Predators to a 4-3 victory over the Pittsburgh Penguins o...
articles.body:
NASHVILLE, Tenn. (AP) — Jayden Struble and Jonathan Marchessault each had a goal and an assist to lead the Nashville Predators to a 4-3 victory over the Pittsburgh Penguins on Saturday.

Filip Forsberg and Reid Schaeffer also scored and Juuse Saros made 21 saves for the Predators, who won for the eighth time in 10 games. Struble broke a 3-all tie at 3:31 of the third period on a tap-in from just outside the crease off a pass from Steven Stamkos, who has a point in five straight.

Samuel Girard, Andrei Kuzmenko and Hendrix Lapierre scored and Sergei Murashov made 25 saves for the Penguins, who have lost four of five and eight of 10 (2-7-1).

Girard scored the first goal at 3:58 of the opening period on a slap shot from above the left circle that deflected off Stamkos' stick before beating Saros high to the far side.

Kuzmenko made it 2-0 with 3:42 remaining in the first, after skating through the slot and beating Saros with a wrist shot for his first goal of the season.

Marchessault halved the Pittsburgh lead with 2:34 left in the period on a one-timer from the left side.

Since missing seven games with a lower-body injury, Marchessault has scored in consecutive games.

Saros was replaced by Justus Annunen briefly in the first after having an issue with a skate blade. Annunen stopped both shots he faced in 2:07 of ice time before Saros returned near the midpoint of the first.

Forsberg made it 2-all at 2:25 of the second, snapping a wrist shot from the left faceoff dot that snuck under Murashov's blocker.

Schaeffer's goal at 6:22 of the second gave Nashville its first lead.

Lapierre tied it at 3 with 6:33 remaining in the second when his wrist shot from the right side through traffic beat Saros on the far side.

Penguins: Visit the Dallas Stars on Sunday.

articles.title: Jaylen Harrell car crash details: What we know about traffic accident that hospitalized Titans pass rusher
articles.summary: Harrell, 24, reportedly lost consciousness after striking his head on the windshield of his rideshare during a wreck on Friday morning.
articles.body:
Titans EDGE Jaylen Harrell remains hospitalized after being involved in a serious car crash in Tampa, the Titans announced on Saturday afternoon.

The wreck took place one day earlier. Preliminary information released by authorities allege that Harrell caused the wreck, having reportedly assaulted the driver of his rideshare prior to it veering off the road.

Harrell, Tennessee's seventh-round pick in the 2024 Draft, was ruled out for the season after sustaining a torn ACL in preseason. He has 38 tackles, 4.5 sacks and a forced fumble in 34 games.

With that, here's what we know so far about Harrell's wreck.

Harrell was hospitalized after being involved in a serious car crash Friday morning. The accident took place in Tampa, Harrell's hometown, on Friday morning. The 24-year-old was placed on injured reserve after tearing his ACL in August.

Tampa police responded to the collision at around 8:45 a.m. ET, per WTSP .

WTSP reported that Harrell was driving as a passenger in the back seat of a rideshare when he "reportedly assaulted the driver while the vehicle was in motion", per the police report.

The driver reportedly swerved, striking a second car before colliding with a utility pole. Harrell was thrown forward in the collision, striking the windshield and losing consciousness, per WTSP.

He was summarily transported to a nearby hospital where he remains under medical supervision. The driver of Harrell's rideshare was treated with minor injuries at the scene. The driver of the second vehicle was left unharmed.

Preliminary information provided by Tampa authorities indicate that Harrell "assaulted the driver" of the Kia Sorento he was riding in on Friday morning, leading to the collision. He remains under medical evaluation in a nearby Tampa hospital.

At present, it's unclear whether Harrell will face charges for his alleged involvement in the collision.

On Saturday, the Titans announced that Harrell was involved in a serious car accident.

"Yesterday, Jaylen Harrell was involved in a serious car accident that resulted in him being taken to the hospital in his hometown of Tampa, Florida," the statement s aid. "We have been in constant communication with Jaylen's family and are still working to gather more information. At this time, Jaylen remains in the hospital and continues to receive care. We ask that Jaylen and his family's privacy be respected at this time. We will provide an update when appropriate."

articles.title: Arizona volleyball drops 4-setter at Utah despite strong outing by Carlie Cisneros
articles.summary: Another competitive match that ends the wrong way for the Wildcats
articles.body:
The Arizona Wildcats have taken sets off or played very competitive three-setters against teams ranked 10th, 11th, 14th, and 32nd in the RPI during Big 12 play. On Saturday, No. 40 Utah was on the schedule. Once again, it was a competitive match that ended in a 3-1 (25-18, 22-25, 25-21, 26-24) loss.

"Other than how we started off the set, the first set—I wasn't too happy with that—I thought we did a good job of staying competitive on the floor," Arizona head coach Rita Stubbs said. "Unfortunately, our skills broke down in certain situations, and coachability wasn't necessarily the best, and they took advantage of it at the right time, but the wrong time for us."

Arizona was especially done in by Utah runs later in sets. That was even the case in the second set, which the Wildcats won.

UA went up 19-12 in the second only to have the Utes go on a five-point run to close the lead to two. The big cushion was the saving grace for the Wildcats. They were able to trade points and mini-runs with Utah down the stretch to win by three points.

Those mid- and late-set runs were their downfall in the third and fourth sets. It didn't take a lot in sets that were so closely contested.

The difference in the third came with the teams tied at 12. Utah went on a three-point run to reach the technical timeout leading 15-12. It never trailed again.

Another three-point run later in the set gave the Utes set point at 24-19. Arizona saved two set points, but it was just one of five occasions when it scored more than one point in a row. Four of those five "runs" were of just two points and the other was three.

The fourth was a back-and-forth affair throughout as Arizona fought to stay in the match. The Wildcats took their first lead at 7-6 and had a four-point lead at the technical timeout.

As was common throughout the match, the timeout helped the team that had been struggling. Utah used a 7-2 run to take the lead at 18-17.

Stubbs called time and Arizona responded with a 4-0 run to go up 21-17. The Wildcats were so close to evening the match.

Once again, the timeout changed the teams' fortunes. The Utes called time and followed with a 3-0 run to tie the set again.

Arizona couldn't string points together after that. The Utes had two 2-0 mini-runs. That was enough to win the set 26-24 and close out the match.

Arizona's outside hitters both carried the team at different times while fighting against some difficult sets. In the early part of the match, junior Carlie Cisneros was the primary scorer as the Utes picked on Destiny Ndam-Simpson in serve receive. Cisneros was aggressive, which Stubbs praised after the match.

Cisneros took more of the serve receive load on as the match progressed, but she still ended with a team-high 14 kills on .278 hitting. Ten digs gave her a double-double. A block assist and her kills tied her for the team lead with 14.5 points.

Ndam-Simpson got stronger as the match progressed. She was second on the team with 12 kills. Her hitting percentage fluctuated wildly throughout. She struggled in the first set with no kills and one hitting error, but she found her game in the second set and continued through the third.

Ndam-Simpson's hitting percentage reached a high of .320 late in the third when she reached her 10th kill of the match. It dropped back to .156 by the end of the match after four hitting errors against just two kills in the final set.

Her serve receive also improved later in the match. She was aced four times, but half of those came in the first set. She was targeted by the Utah serve a team-high 39 times.

"Dez struggled on the first one, but got better on the second one," Stubbs said. "And so what I told her was, whatever you're saying to yourself on the second pass, say it on the first one. You know, you're just trying to find different things to make them laugh or be restful because sometimes they tend to beat themselves up for the error that they make and we're always trying to teach them was that a good error or a bad error. So the fact that she was able to self correct without us being able to tell her anything—because unless you call a time out you can't really get it there—that's a good sign. Earlier in the year, that would have resulted in three, four of them in a row potentially."

Arizona got significant contributions from its middle blockers. Journey Tucker was especially strong on the offensive side in the early going. She had five kills on .333 hitting in the match, but four of those were in the first two sets. Her block picked up as the match progressed. She ended with four total blocks including one solo. Three of the four came after the first set.

It was a good weekend overall for Tucker, although her blocking numbers weren't as big this time as they were in the last match against Utah. When the Utes came to Tucson, Tucker had nine blocks. She only had one block at BYU on Thursday, but that's not the only job of a middle blocker.

"She was a great blocker from pin to pin [at BYU]," Stubbs said. "I don't think she was the best in terms of blocking the middle, but she was touching balls, making the hitters do something different, which made our defense better, which is what you would want. And what I told her was, I said it's pretty frustrating to do that and it's not statted anywhere. That's why being a middle blocker sometimes is hard because you only think your reward comes when you get the block, but if you're directing it to the defender, you've done your job."

Fellow middle blocker Marina Vosloo ended with seven kills, although they were paired with five hitting errors. She tied for second on the team with two total blocks. Between Vosloo and Tucker, the middles contributed 26 percent of the Wildcats' kills and 27 percent of their total points.

The Utes were able to contain right side hitter Kennedy Osunsanmi , who has been one of Arizona's primary offensive weapons this season with 2.09 kills per set. The opposite had three kills on a negative hitting percentage against Utah, but she contributed in other areas. She ended with a season-high six digs and had two total blocks.

In many situations, Stubbs will substitute a player out if she's starting to struggle physically, mentally, or emotionally. It wasn't a possibility on Saturday.

Backup opposite Renee Jones , who is fourth on the team with 1.60 kills per set, was unavailable. She had a visit to the emergency room for IV fluids on Friday due to a bout with the flu. She was not on the bench.

"When you're Type 1 diabetic, it becomes something that you become a little bit more aware and conscious of," Stubbs said.

On the other side of the availability story, the Wildcats got defensive specialist Brenna Ginder back this weekend. She has been out since getting elbowed in the face by a teammate against Houston on Oct. 30. She was reintroduced as a serving specialist against BYU on Thursday and appeared in all four sets against Utah.

"She went in and she mixed it up as a server," Stubbs said. "I know she missed that one, which she beat herself up for that, but after that, she went back and she was aggressive. You know, you're gonna lose some, win some, lose some. My goal is for us to always serve the ball out if we serve an error versus in the net, and so I was pleased with that. So I was happy. It was nice having her back."

articles.title: New report reveals Puka Nacua's lengthy recovery timeline after MCL surgery
articles.summary: Puka Nacua will be sidelined 4-5 months after having surgery on his MCL, which is longer than Sean McVay suggested.
articles.body:
When Sean McVay announced that Puka Nacua decided to have surgery on his knee to repair his MCL , he said the Los Angeles Rams ' star receiver would be out "a couple months." It turns out Nacua will be sidelined much longer than that.

Adam Schefter of ESPN reported on Saturday that Nacua will be out 4-5 months following MCL surgery. That definitively rules him out for the postseason, if the Rams make it that far.

The surgery, which was performed by Rams doctor Neal ElAttrache, is expected to have Nacua ready for the start of the 2027 season. According to Schefter, three doctors recommended that Nacua have surgery on his knee, and that everything "checked out clean aside from the MCL," which is good news.

Nacua suffered the injury in Week 9 against the Washington Commanders , taking a shot to his knee on the final offensive snap when he took a jet sweep for 5 yards on third-and-11. McVay admitted he second-guessed himself over that call, which was Nacua's 15th touch of the game.

With Nacua's season over, he finishes the year with 70 catches for 715 yards and four touchdowns in only seven games. It's the fewest receptions and yards he's had in a season in his career, but he set a new career high in receptions per game (10.0) and had his second-most yards per game (102.1).

articles.title: Police investigating whether Titans’ Jaylen Harrell assaulted driver before Florida crash
articles.summary: Tennessee Titans’ Jaylen Harrell was hospitalized following a serious car crash, and police said Saturday that they were investigating whether he assaulted a rideshare driver.
articles.body: Tennessee Titans defensive end Jaylen Harrell was hospitalized in Florida following a serious car crash, and police said Saturday that they were investigating whether he assaulted a rideshare driver. Harrell was in his hometown of Tampa when the crash occurred Friday morning. The Titans said in a statement that he was continuing to receive care in the hospital and they were in constant communication with his family. Tampa Police said in a statement that Harrell was a passenger in the back seat of a white Kia Sorento “when he reportedly assaulted the driver while the vehicle was in motion.” The driver, a man in his mid-30s, swerved and struck a second vehicle before colliding with a utility pole. Harrell was thrown forward, struck the windshield and lost consciousness, the statement said. The driver had minor injuries and was treated at the scene, according to police. The driver of the second vehicle, a woman in her early 50s, was not hurt. The 24-year-old Harrell has not played for the Titans this season. He injured his ACL during the preseason and was placed on season-ending injured reserve. The Titans asked for privacy for Harrell and his family and said they would “provide an update when appropriate.” Tennessee selected Harrell in the seventh round of the 2024 draft out of Michigan. He finished his rookie season with 13 combined tackles and had 25 last season. He had 4 1/2 sacks and a forced fumble in 2025. Harrell’s father, James, also played eight seasons in the NFL.

articles.title: España conquista la plata en kata masculino en el Mundial de Hangzhou
articles.standfirst: El equipo femenino de kumite se queda a las puertas del podio
articles.summary: El equipo femenino de kumite se queda a las puertas del podio
articles.body: España se ha colgado la plata en kata masculino en el Mundial de karate por equipos que se celebra en Hangzhou (China). El equipo femenino de kumite se ha quedado a las puertas de subir también al podio. El equipo masculino de kata, integrado por Raúl Martín, Iván Martín, Alejandro Galán y Antonio Lozano, bajo la dirección del seleccionador nacional José Antonio Alburquerque, se ha proclamado subcampeón tras caer ante Japón en la final. El conjunto español superó con solvencia la fase de grupos y mostró su gran nivel técnico a lo largo de las eliminatorias confirmando que nuestro país sigue siendo un referente mundial en kata, la disciplina en la que Sandra Sánchez fue oro olímpico en Tokio 2020 y Damián Quintero, plata. El equipo masculino español mejora el bronce conseguido en la anterior edición de la Karate World Cup, celebrada en Pamplona, y da un nuevo paso en su trayectoria internacional. Por su parte, el equipo femenino de kumite, integrado por María Torres, Indira Zúñiga, Isabel Nieto, Julia Just e Irene Fernández, bajo la dirección del seleccionador nacional Iván Leal, cayó ante China en la lucha por la medalla de bronce y acabó en cuarta posición. Las españolas han protagonizado un igualadísimo encuentro que ha terminado con un resultado de 1-1, resuelto a favor del conjunto anfitrión. España llegaba a la lucha por las medallas tras superar a Argelia en cuartos de final por 2-1 y caer ante Túnez en semifinales. El equipo femenino de kata, compuesto por Paola García Lozano, Abril Angulo, Carla Guardeño e Irene Yao Alcaraz, junto al seleccionador nacional Fran Salazar, superó la fase de grupos con autoridad tras vencer a Brasil, Hong Kong, Montenegro y Marruecos, pero perdió ante Egipto en cuartos de final.

Will Bhayshul Tuten play against the Giants ?

Star or sit Bhayshul Tuten in fantasy football?
